text: SELF-ESTEEM, n. An erroneous appraisement.
source: Ambrose Bierce, The Devil's Dictionary (1911).
sourceRaw: [[Ambrose Bierce]], ''The Devil's Dictionary'' (1911).
author: Ambrose Bierce
textKo: 자존감, 명사. 잘못된 평가.

text: It would be hard to name a more certain sign of poor self-esteem than the need to perceive some other group as inferior.
source: Nathaniel Branden, The Six Pillars of Self-Esteem (1994)
sourceRaw: [[Nathaniel Branden]], ''The Six Pillars of Self-Esteem'' (1994)
author: Nathaniel Branden
textKo: 낮은 자존감의 가장 확실한 표지는 어떤 다른 집단을 열등하다고 여길 필요를 느끼는 것이다.

text: Perform anonymous service. Whenever we do good for others anonymously, our sense of intrinsic worth and self-respect increases. … Selfless service has always been one of the most powerful methods of influence.
source: Stephen Covey, Principle-Centered Leadership, ch. 11 (1992)
sourceRaw: [[Stephen Covey]], ''Principle-Centered Leadership'', ch. 11 (1992)
author: Stephen Covey
textKo: 익명으로 봉사하라. 익명으로 남을 위한 선을 행할 때마다 우리의 내재적 가치감과 자존감은 커진다… 무사의 봉사는 늘 가장 강력한 영향력의 방법 중 하나였다.

text: Self-respect is a question of recognizing that anything worth having has a price.
source: Joan Didion, "On Self-Respect", in Slouching Towards Bethlehem (1968)
sourceRaw: [[Joan Didion]], "On Self-Respect", in ''[[w:Slouching Towards Bethlehem|Slouching Towards Bethlehem]]'' (1968)
author: Joan Didion
textKo: 자존이란, 가질 만한 가치가 있는 것에는 모두 대가가 있다는 사실을 인정하는 문제다.

text: The willingness to accept responsibility for one's own life is the source from which self-respect springs.
source: Joan Didion, "On Self-Respect", in Slouching Towards Bethlehem (1968)
sourceRaw: [[Joan Didion]], "On Self-Respect", in ''[[w:Slouching Towards Bethlehem|Slouching Towards Bethlehem]]'' (1968)
author: Joan Didion
textKo: 자기 삶에 대한 책임을 기꺼이 받아들이는 것 — 그것이 자존이 솟아나는 원천이다.

text: Self-esteem is the greatest sickness known to man or woman because it's conditional.
source: Albert Ellis, "A Guide to Rational Living" (1961)
sourceRaw: [[Albert Ellis]],  "A Guide to Rational Living" (1961)
author: Albert Ellis
textKo: 자존감은 남녀에게 알려진 가장 큰 병이다. 왜냐하면 그것은 조건적이기 때문이다.

text: Nothing is better for self-esteem than survival.
source: Martha Gellhorn, Travels with Myself and Another: A Memoir (1978)
sourceRaw: [[Martha Gellhorn]], ''Travels with Myself and Another: A Memoir'' (1978)
author: Martha Gellhorn
textKo: 생존만큼 자존감에 좋은 것은 없다.

text: Above all things, one should maintain his self-respect, and there is but one way to do that, and that is to live in accordance with your highest ideal.
source: Robert G. Ingersoll, The trial of Charles B. Reynolds for blasphemy (1887)
sourceRaw: [[Robert G. Ingersoll]], The trial of [[w:Charles B. Reynolds|Charles B. Reynolds]] for blasphemy (1887)
author: Robert G. Ingersoll
textKo: 무엇보다도 자존을 지켜야 한다. 그 길은 단 하나, 자신의 가장 높은 이상에 따라 사는 것이다.

text: Self-respect — The secure feeling that no one, as yet, is suspicious.
source: H. L. Mencken, A Mencken Chrestomathy (1949)
sourceRaw: [[H. L. Mencken]], ''A Mencken Chrestomathy'' (1949)
author: H. L. Mencken
textKo: 자존이란 — 아직 아무도 의심하지 않고 있다는 안도의 감정.

text: People need self-respect, but self-respect must be earned -- it cannot be self-respect if it's not earned -- and the only way to earn anything is to achieve it in the face of the possibility of failing.
source: Charles Murray, Coming Apart: The State of White America, 1960-2010. Crown Forum (2012); ISBN10: 0307453421; ISBN13: 9780307453426
sourceRaw: [[Charles Murray (author)|Charles Murray]], ''[http://www.goodreads.com/work/quotes/16997889 Coming Apart: The State of White America, 1960-2010]''. Crown Forum (2012); ISBN10: 0307453421; ISBN13: 9780307453426
author: Charles Murray (author)
textKo: 사람에게는 자존이 필요하지만, 자존은 반드시 얻어져야 한다 — 얻어지지 않은 것은 자존이 아니다. 그리고 무언가를 얻는 유일한 길은 실패의 가능성 앞에서 그것을 성취하는 것이다.

text: Never violate the sacredness of your individual self-respect. Be true to your own mind and conscience, your heart and your soul. So only can you be true to God.
source: Theodore Parker, Two Sermons, Sermon II: Of the Position and Duty of a Minister (1853).
sourceRaw: [[Theodore Parker]], ''Two Sermons'', Sermon II: Of the Position and Duty of a Minister (1853).
author: Theodore Parker
textKo: 너의 개인적 자존의 신성함을 결코 침해하지 마라. 너의 마음과 양심에, 너의 심장과 영혼에 충실하라. 그래야 신께도 충실할 수 있다.

text: I need no warrant for being, and no word of sanction upon my being. I am the warrant and the sanction.
source: Ayn Rand, Anthem (1938)
sourceRaw: [[Ayn Rand]], ''[[w:Anthem (novella)|Anthem]]'' (1938)
author: Ayn Rand
textKo: 내 존재에 어떤 영장도, 어떤 인가의 말도 필요치 않다. 나 자신이 그 영장이며 인가다.

text: Honor is self-esteem made visible in action.
source: Ayn Rand, The Ayn Rand Letter (1971–1976)
sourceRaw: [[Ayn Rand]], ''The Ayn Rand Letter'' (1971–1976)
author: Ayn Rand
textKo: 명예란 행동으로 가시화된 자존감이다.

text: Anything that encourages pauperism, anything that relaxes the manly fiber and lowers self-respect, is an unmixed evil.
source: Theodore Roosevelt, Civic Helpfulness, first published in the "Century", October, 1900. Published in The Strenuous Life: Essays and Addresses (1910)
sourceRaw: [[Theodore Roosevelt]], ''Civic Helpfulness'', first published in the "Century", October, 1900. Published in ''[[The Strenuous Life: Essays and Addresses]]'' (1910)
author: Theodore Roosevelt
textKo: 걸식을 부추기는 모든 것, 사내다운 기상을 풀어버리고 자존을 떨어뜨리는 모든 것은 순전한 악이다.

text: The wise treat self-respect as non-negotiable, and will not trade it for health or wealth or anything else.
source: Thomas Szasz, The Second Sin, p. 56 (1973)
sourceRaw: [[Thomas Szasz]], ''The Second Sin'', p. 56 (1973)
author: Thomas Szasz
textKo: 지혜로운 자는 자존을 협상할 수 없는 것으로 여기며, 건강이나 부, 그 무엇과도 바꾸지 않는다.

text: Danger breeds best on too much confidence.
source: Pierre Corneille, Le Cid (1636).
sourceRaw: [[Pierre Corneille]], ''Le Cid'' (1636).
author: Pierre Corneille
textKo: 위험은 지나친 자신감 위에서 가장 잘 자란다.

text: According to Freud (who was speaking from experience, since he was his mother’s darling), spoiled children have a confidence that stays with them all their lives.
source: Robert Greene, The Art of Seduction (2001)
sourceRaw: [[Robert Greene (American author)|Robert Greene]], ''The Art of Seduction'' (2001)
author: Robert Greene (American author)
textKo: 프로이트에 따르면(그는 어머니의 사랑을 듬뿍 받은 자기 경험에서 한 말이다), 응석받이 아이들은 평생을 따라가는 자신감을 갖는다고 한다.

text: As is our confidence, so is our capacity.
source: William Hazlitt, Characteristics (1823).
sourceRaw: [[William Hazlitt]], ''Characteristics'' (1823).
author: William Hazlitt
textKo: 우리의 자신감만큼이 우리의 역량이다.

text: Where men are the most sure and arrogant, they are commonly the most mistaken.
source: David Hume, in An Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals (1751), § 9.13 : Conclusion, Pt. 1
sourceRaw: [[David Hume]], in ''An Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals'' (1751), § 9.13 : Conclusion, Pt. 1
author: David Hume
textKo: 사람들은 가장 확신하고 거만할 때 흔히 가장 크게 틀린다.

text: It is wonderful how some words ever were invented, for they express what does not exist—confidence is among the number; confidence is what no human being ever really had in another.
source: Letitia Elizabeth Landon, Francesca Carrara, Volume I, Chapter 4 (1834).
sourceRaw: [[Letitia Elizabeth Landon]], ''Francesca Carrara'', Volume I, Chapter 4 (1834).
author: Letitia Elizabeth Landon
textKo: 어떤 말들이 어떻게 만들어졌는지 놀랍다. 그 말들은 실재하지 않는 것을 가리키니. '자신감'도 그중 하나다. 자신감이란 어떤 인간도 다른 인간에게 진실로 가져본 적 없는 것이다.

text: Ignorance and confidence are constant companions
source: John McAfee, Into the Heart of Truth (2001).
sourceRaw: [[John McAfee]], ''Into the Heart of Truth'' (2001).
author: John McAfee
textKo: 무지와 자신감은 늘 동행하는 짝이다.

text: Confidence is a plant of slow growth in an aged bosom.
source: William Pitt, 1st Earl of Chatham, speech, Jan. 14, 1766, reported in Bartlett's Familiar Quotations, 10th ed. (1919).
sourceRaw: [[William Pitt, 1st Earl of Chatham]], speech, Jan. 14, 1766, reported in ''Bartlett's Familiar Quotations'', 10th ed. (1919).
author: William Pitt, 1st Earl of Chatham
textKo: 신뢰는 나이 든 가슴 속에서 더디게 자라는 식물이다.

text: I have confidence in fools... self-confidence is what my friends call it.
source: Edgar Allan Poe, Marginalia (November 1844).
sourceRaw: [[Edgar Allan Poe]], ''Marginalia'' (November 1844).
author: Edgar Allan Poe
textKo: 나는 바보들을 신뢰한다… 내 친구들은 그걸 자신감이라 부른다.

text: Confidence... thrives on honesty, on honor, on the sacredness of obligations, on faithful protection and on unselfish performance. Without them it cannot live.
source: Franklin D. Roosevelt, First Inaugural Address (4 March 1933).
sourceRaw: [[Franklin D. Roosevelt]], [[s:Franklin Roosevelt's First Inaugural Address|First Inaugural Address]] (4 March 1933).
author: Franklin D. Roosevelt
textKo: 신뢰는… 정직, 명예, 의무의 신성함, 충실한 보호, 사심 없는 수행 위에서 번성한다. 이것들 없이는 신뢰는 살 수 없다.

text: I see before me the statue of a celebrated minister, who said that confidence was a plant of slow growth. But I believe, however gradual may be the growth of confidence, that of credit requires still more time to arrive at maturity.
source: Benjamin Disraeli, speech (Nov. 9, 1867).
sourceRaw: [[Benjamin Disraeli]], speech (Nov. 9, 1867).
workTitle: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
author: Benjamin Disraeli
sectionPath: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
textKo: 내 앞에는 어느 유명 정치인의 동상이 서 있다. 그는 신뢰가 더디게 자라는 식물이라 말했다. 그러나 나는 믿는다 — 신뢰가 아무리 더디게 자라더라도, 신용은 그것이 성숙에 이르기까지 더 오랜 시간이 걸린다.

text: Your wisdom is consum'd in confidence.Do not go forth to-day.
source: William Shakespeare, Julius Cæsar (1599), Act II, scene 2, line 49.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Julius Caesar (play)|Julius Cæsar]]'' (1599), Act II, scene 2, line 49.
workTitle: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
author: William Shakespeare
sectionPath: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
textKo: 너의 지혜는 자신감으로 인해 다 소진되었다. 오늘은 나가지 마라.

text: I would have some confidence with you that decerns you nearly.
source: William Shakespeare, Much Ado About Nothing (1598-99), Act III, scene 5, line 3.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Much Ado About Nothing]]'' (1598-99), Act III, scene 5, line 3.
workTitle: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
author: William Shakespeare
sectionPath: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
textKo: 너에게 깊이 관련된 일을 두고 너와 은밀히 의논하고 싶다.

text: 'Tis pride, rank pride, and haughtiness of soul: I think the Romans call it Stoicism.
source: Joseph Addison, Cato, A Tragedy (1713), Act I, scene 4.
sourceRaw: [[Joseph Addison]], ''Cato, A Tragedy'' (1713), Act I, scene 4.
author: Joseph Addison
textKo: 그것은 교만, 노골적인 교만, 영혼의 거만함이다. 로마인들은 그것을 스토아주의라 부른다고 하더라.

text: The soul, secured in her existence, smiles At the drawn dagger, and defies its point.
source: Joseph Addison, Cato, A Tragedy (1713), Act V, scene 1.
sourceRaw: [[Joseph Addison]], ''Cato, A Tragedy'' (1713), Act V, scene 1.
author: Joseph Addison
textKo: 자기 존재 안에 안전한 영혼은, 뽑힌 단검 앞에서도 미소 짓고, 그 끝을 비웃는다.

text: The brave man is not he who feels no fear,For that were stupid and irrational;But he, whose noble soul its fear subdues,And bravely dares the danger nature shrinks from.
source: Joanna Baillie, Count Basil (1798), Act III, scene 1, line 151.
sourceRaw: [[Joanna Baillie]], ''Count Basil'' (1798), Act III, scene 1, line 151.
author: Joanna Baillie
textKo: 용감한 자는 두려움을 느끼지 않는 자가 아니니, 그렇다면 어리석고 비이성적일 뿐이다. 그는 자신의 두려움을 굴복시키고, 본성이 움츠리는 위험을 용감히 마주하는 고귀한 영혼의 사람이다.

text: Go to the edge of the cliff and jump off. Build your wings on the way down.
source: Ray Bradbury, Brown Daily Herald (March 24, 1995).
sourceRaw: [[Ray Bradbury]], ''Brown Daily Herald'' (March 24, 1995).
author: Ray Bradbury
textKo: 절벽 끝으로 가서 뛰어내려라. 떨어지는 동안 너의 날개를 만들어라.

text: Walk on with courage and bravery. Go on working to improve humankind and establish the Path of Truth. (…) Fight for truth! To face life you must have great courage every day.
source: Haidakhan Babaji, The Teachings of Babaji, 16 January 1983.
sourceRaw: [[Haidakhan Babaji]], ''The Teachings of Babaji'', 16 January 1983.
author: Haidakhan Babaji
textKo: 용기와 담대함으로 걸어가라. 인류를 향상시키고 진리의 길을 세우는 일을 계속하라. (…) 진리를 위해 싸워라! 삶을 마주하려면 매일 큰 용기가 있어야 한다.

text: Now people with courage are needed. It is better to die, facing life with courage. To live as a coward is shameful – it is better that the coward drown himself in the river. (…) Awake! Arise! Be brave!
source: Haidakhan Babaji, The Teachings of Babaji, 5 July 1983.
sourceRaw: [[Haidakhan Babaji]], ''The Teachings of Babaji'', 5 July 1983.
author: Haidakhan Babaji
textKo: 이제는 용기 있는 사람들이 필요하다. 용기로 삶을 마주하다 죽는 것이 낫다. 겁쟁이로 사는 것은 부끄러운 일이며 — 겁쟁이는 차라리 강물에 몸을 던지는 편이 낫다. (…) 깨어나라! 일어나라! 용감하라!

text: When a man is fearless, no man can stand against him in battle – either a battle in material life or in spiritual life. He is victorious in all battles of life.
source: Haidakhan Babaji, The Teachings of Babaji, 29 October 1983.
sourceRaw: [[Haidakhan Babaji]], ''The Teachings of Babaji'', 29 October 1983.
author: Haidakhan Babaji
textKo: 두려움 없는 자에게는 어떤 사람도 전장에서 맞설 수 없다 — 물질적 삶의 전장에서든 영적 삶의 전장에서든. 그는 삶의 모든 싸움에서 승리한다.

text: All doubt is cowardice — all trust is brave.
source: Edward Bulwer-Lytton, King Arthur (1848-9), Book XII, Chapter XXVIII.
sourceRaw: [[Edward Bulwer-Lytton]], ''King Arthur'' (1848-9), Book XII, Chapter XXVIII.
author: Edward Bulwer-Lytton
textKo: 모든 의심은 비겁이고, 모든 신뢰는 용감하다.

text: The French courage proceeds from vanity — the German from phlegm — the Turkish from fanaticism & opium — the Spanish from pride — the English from coolness — the Dutch from obstinacy — the Russian from insensibility — but the Italian from anger.
source: George Gordon Noel Byron (1788–1824), British poet. in a letter to his publisher John Murray (1820).
sourceRaw: [[George Gordon Noel Byron]] (1788–1824), British poet. in a letter to his publisher John Murray (1820).
author: George Gordon Noel Byron
textKo: 프랑스인의 용기는 허영에서, 독일인의 용기는 침착함에서, 터키인의 용기는 광신과 아편에서, 스페인인의 용기는 자존심에서, 영국인의 용기는 냉정함에서, 네덜란드인의 용기는 고집에서, 러시아인의 용기는 무감각에서 오나, 이탈리아인의 용기는 분노에서 온다.

text: And each man stands with his face in the lightOf his own drawn sword,Ready to do what a hero can.
source: Elizabeth Barrett Browning, Napoleon III in Italy (1860), VIII.
sourceRaw: [[Elizabeth Barrett Browning]], ''Napoleon III in Italy'' (1860), VIII.
author: Elizabeth Barrett Browning
textKo: 그리고 각 사람은 자신이 뽑은 칼의 빛에 얼굴을 두고, 영웅이 할 수 있는 일을 할 준비를 한다.

text: Valour lies just halfway between rashness and cowheartedness.
source: Miguel de Cervantes, Don Quixote (1605-15)
sourceRaw: [[Miguel de Cervantes]], ''Don Quixote'' (1605-15)
author: Miguel de Cervantes
textKo: 용맹은 무모함과 비겁함의 정확한 중간에 있다.

text: There are seasons, in human affairs, of inward and outward revolution, when new depths seem to be broken up in the soul, when new wants are unfolded in multitudes, and a new and undefined good is thirsted for. There are periods when...to dare, is the highest wisdom.
source: William Ellery Channing, The Union (1829).
sourceRaw: [[William Ellery Channing]], ''The Union'' (1829).
author: William Ellery Channing
textKo: 인간사에는 안팎의 혁명의 시기가 있다. 영혼에 새로운 심연이 깨어나고, 다수에게 새로운 욕구가 펼쳐지며, 정의되지 않은 새로운 선이 갈망되는 시기. 그런 때엔… 감행하는 것이 가장 큰 지혜다.

text: Courage is almost a contradiction in terms. It means a strong desire to live taking the form of a readiness to die.
source: G.K. Chesterton, Orthodoxy, Chapter 6 (1909).
sourceRaw: [[G.K. Chesterton]], ''Orthodoxy'', Chapter 6 (1909).
author: G.K. Chesterton
textKo: 용기란 거의 용어의 모순이다. 그것은 죽음을 받아들이는 형태를 띤, 살고자 하는 강한 열망이다.

text: Courage is what others can't see, what is never affirmed. It is made of what you have thrown away and then come back for.
source: Leonard Cohen. From Leonard Cohen’s journals. As quoted in: Zeus Ghosh (June 30, 2022): Hallelujah: Leonard Cohen, A Journey, A Song (2021) Review: A tryst with the God of Songs. In: High on Films. Archived from the original on March 5, 2023. author: Leonard Cohen
textKo: 용기란 남에게 보이지 않는 것, 확인받지 못하는 것이다. 그것은 네가 버렸다가 다시 찾으러 돌아간 것들로 만들어진다.

text: It may often be noticed, the less virtuous people are, the more they shrink away from the slightest whiff of the odour of un-sanctity. The good are ever the most charitable, the pure are the most brave.
source: Dinah Craik, A Woman's Thoughts About Women (1858), Ch. 11.
sourceRaw: [[Dinah Craik]], ''A Woman's Thoughts About Women'' (1858), Ch. 11.
author: Dinah Craik
textKo: 흔히 보이는 일이지만, 덜 덕망 있는 사람일수록 신성하지 않다는 아주 희미한 냄새조차 피하려 한다. 선한 자는 늘 가장 너그럽고, 순수한 자는 가장 용감하다.

text: Whistling to keep myself from being afraid.
source: John Dryden, Amphitryon (1690), Act III, scene 1.
sourceRaw: [[John Dryden]], ''Amphitryon'' (1690), Act III, scene 1.
author: John Dryden
textKo: 두려움에 사로잡히지 않으려고 휘파람을 분다.

text: Courage is the price that life exacts for granting peace.The soul that knows it not, know no releaseFrom little things;Knows not the livid loneliness of fear,Nor mountain heights where bitter joy can hearThe sound of wings.
source: Amelia Earhart, Courage (1927).
sourceRaw: [[Amelia Earhart]], ''Courage'' (1927).
author: Amelia Earhart
textKo: 용기는 삶이 평화를 허락하는 대가로 요구하는 것이다. 그것을 모르는 영혼은 사소한 것에서 결코 풀려나지 못하며, 두려움의 시퍼런 외로움도, 쓰디쓴 기쁨이 날갯짓을 들을 수 있는 산정도 알지 못한다.

text: Courage charms us, because it indicates that a man loves an idea better than all things in the world, that he is thinking neither of his bed, nor his dinner, nor his money, but will venture all to put in act the invisible thought of his mind.
source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Journals, entry in 1859 (1909-1914).
sourceRaw: [[Ralph Waldo Emerson]], ''Journals'', entry in 1859 (1909-1914).
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
textKo: 용기는 우리를 매료시킨다. 그것은 한 사람이 세상의 그 어떤 것보다 하나의 사상을 더 사랑한다는 것, 침대도 저녁식사도 돈도 생각지 않고, 마음속 보이지 않는 생각을 행동으로 옮기기 위해 모든 것을 걸겠다는 것을 보여주기 때문이다.

text: A great part of courage is the courage of having done the thing before.
source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, "Culture," The Conduct of Life (1860).
sourceRaw: [[Ralph Waldo Emerson]], "Culture," ''The Conduct of Life'' (1860).
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
textKo: 용기의 큰 부분은 이전에 그 일을 해냈다는 사실에서 오는 용기다.

text: 'Tis said that courage is common, but the immense esteem in which it is held proves it to be rare. Animal resistance, the instinct of the male animal when cornered, is no doubt common; but the pure article, courage with eyes, courage with conduct, self-possession at the cannon's mouth, cheerfulness in lonely adherence to the right, is the endowment of elevated characters.
source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, "Courage," Society and Solitude (1870).
sourceRaw: [[Ralph Waldo Emerson]], "Courage," ''Society and Solitude'' (1870).
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
textKo: 용기가 흔하다고들 하지만, 그것이 받는 큰 존경이 곧 용기가 드물다는 증거다. 동물적 저항, 궁지에 몰린 수컷의 본능은 흔할지 모른다. 그러나 진짜 용기 — 눈을 뜬 용기, 절제된 용기, 포구 앞에서의 침착함, 옳음을 향한 외로운 충실함의 명랑함 — 이는 고귀한 인격의 천부적 자질이다.

text: It is plain that there is no separate essence called courage, no cup or cell in the brain, no vessel in the heart containing drops or atoms that make or give this virtue; but it is the right or healthy state of every man, when he is free to do that which is constitutional to him to do.
source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, "Courage," Society and Solitude.
sourceRaw: [[Ralph Waldo Emerson]], "Courage," ''Society and Solitude''.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
textKo: 용기라는 별개의 본질은 없으며, 뇌 속에 그 잔이나 방이 있는 것도, 심장 속에 이 덕을 만들거나 부여하는 방울이나 원자가 담긴 그릇이 있는 것도 아니다. 용기란, 인간이 본래 그에게 맞는 일을 자유로이 할 때 그가 도달하는 '바르고 건강한 상태'일 뿐이다.

text: Be scared. You can’t help that. But don’t be afraid. Ain’t nothing in the woods going to hurt you unless you corner it, or it smells that you are afraid. A bear or a deer, too, has got to be scared of a coward the same as a brave man has got to be.
source: William Faulkner, “The Bear” in The Saturday Evening Post (May 9, 1942).
sourceRaw: [[William Faulkner]], “The Bear” in ''The Saturday Evening Post'' (May 9, 1942).
author: William Faulkner
textKo: 무서워해도 좋다. 그건 어쩔 수 없다. 그러나 두려워하지는 마라. 숲속 어떤 것도, 네가 그것을 궁지에 몰거나 네가 두려워한다는 냄새를 맡지 않는 한 너를 해치지 않는다. 곰이든 사슴이든 용감한 사람만큼이나 겁쟁이를 무서워해야 한다.

text: People talk of the courage of convictions, but in actual life a man's duty to his family may make a rigid course seem a selfish indulgence of his own righteousness.
source: F. Scott Fitzgerald, "The Four Fists", Flappers and Philosophers (1920).
sourceRaw: [[F. Scott Fitzgerald]], "The Four Fists", ''Flappers and Philosophers'' (1920).
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
textKo: 신념의 용기를 말하지만, 실제 삶에서는 가족에 대한 의무가 어떤 경직된 길을 자신의 의로움을 향한 이기적 탐닉처럼 보이게 만들 때도 있다.

text: Either life entails courage, or it ceases to be life.
source: E.M. Forster, Pharos and Pharillon, "The Poetry of C.P. Cavafy" (1923).
sourceRaw: [[E.M. Forster]], ''Pharos and Pharillon'', "The Poetry of C.P. Cavafy"  (1923).
author: E.M. Forster
textKo: 삶이 용기를 요구하지 않는다면, 그것은 삶이기를 멈춘다.

text: Courage is of the heart by derivation,And great it is. But fear is of the soul.
source: Robert Frost, A Masque of Mercy (1947).
sourceRaw: [[Robert Frost]], ''A Masque of Mercy'' (1947).
author: Robert Frost
textKo: 용기는 그 어원상 심장의 것이며, 위대하다. 그러나 두려움은 영혼의 것이다.

text: Courage is in the air in bracing whiffsBetter than all the stalemate an's and ifs.
source: Robert Frost, For John F. Kennedy His Inauguration (1960).
sourceRaw: [[Robert Frost]], ''For John F. Kennedy His Inauguration'' (1960).
author: Robert Frost
textKo: 용기는 상쾌한 바람 속에 떠 있다 — 망설이는 만약과 만일의 모든 교착보다 더 낫다.

text: Courage is contagious. When a brave man takes a stand, the spines of others are often stiffened.
source: Billy Graham, "A Time for Moral Courage" Reader's Digest (July 1964).
sourceRaw: [[Billy Graham]], "A Time for Moral Courage" Reader's Digest (July 1964).
author: Billy Graham
textKo: 용기는 전염된다. 한 용감한 사람이 입장을 정하면, 다른 사람들의 등뼈도 흔히 곧추선다.

text: It is when we all play safe that we create a world of utmost insecurity. It is when we all play safe that fatality will lead us to our doom. It is in the "dark shade of courage" alone that the spell can be broken.
source: Dag Hammarskjöld, Servant of Peace : A Selection of the Speeches and Statements of Dag Hammarskjöld, Secretary General of the United Nations (1962), p. 107.
sourceRaw: [[Dag Hammarskjöld]], ''Servant of Peace : A Selection of the Speeches and Statements of Dag Hammarskjöld, Secretary General of the United Nations'' (1962), p. 107.
author: Dag Hammarskjöld
textKo: 우리 모두가 안전한 선택만 할 때, 우리는 가장 큰 불안의 세상을 만들어낸다. 우리 모두가 안전만 추구할 때, 운명은 우리를 파멸로 인도한다. 오직 '용기의 어두운 그림자' 안에서만 그 주문은 깨질 수 있다.

text: Courage is the ability to ignore your options.
source: Tom Heehler, The Well-Spoken Thesaurus (March, 2011).
sourceRaw: [[Tom Heehler]], ''The Well-Spoken Thesaurus'' (March, 2011).
author: Tom Heehler
textKo: 용기란, 자신의 선택지를 무시할 수 있는 능력이다.

text: My darling girl, when are you going to realize that being normal is not necessarily a virtue? It rather denotes a lack of courage.
source: Alice Hoffman Practical Magic (1995)
sourceRaw: [[Alice Hoffman]] Practical Magic (1995)
author: Alice Hoffman
textKo: 내 사랑하는 아이야, 너는 언제쯤 깨달을 거니 — '정상'이라는 게 꼭 미덕은 아니라는 걸. 오히려 그것은 용기의 결여를 가리킬 뿐이라는 걸.

text: The onward march of the human race requires that the heights around it constantly blaze with noble lessons of courage. Deeds of daring dazzle history and form one of man's guiding lights.
source: Victor Hugo, Les Misérables (1862).
sourceRaw: [[Victor Hugo]], ''[[Les Misérables]]'' (1862).
author: Victor Hugo
textKo: 인류의 전진의 행진은, 주변의 고지대가 끊임없이 용기의 고귀한 가르침으로 타오를 것을 요구한다. 감히 행한 행위들은 역사를 눈부시게 하며, 인간의 길잡이 등불 중 하나가 된다.

text: Courage, of all national qualities, is the most precarious; because it is exerted only at intervals, and by a few in every nation; whereas industry, knowledge, civility, may be of constant and universal use, and for several ages, may become habitual to the whole people.
source: David Hume, Of National Characters, part I, essay XXI (1758).
sourceRaw: [[David Hume]], ''Of National Characters'',  part I, essay XXI (1758).
author: David Hume
textKo: 모든 국가적 자질 중에서 용기는 가장 불안정하다. 그것은 단지 간헐적으로, 각 국가의 소수에 의해서만 발휘되는 반면, 근면·지식·예의는 끊임없이 보편적으로 쓰일 수 있고, 여러 세대에 걸쳐 온 민족의 습성이 될 수 있기 때문이다.

text: [Deprogramming survivor Toru Goto] teaches us that resilience is not a trait, but a choice. That faith is not weakness, but armor. That freedom is not always granted—sometimes, it must be reclaimed.
source: Massimo Introvigne, "The Battle for the Soul: Toru Goto’s Harrowing Tale of Captivity and Courage", Bitter Winter (August 6, 2025)
sourceRaw: [[Massimo Introvigne]], [https://bitterwinter.org/the-battle-for-the-soul-toru-gotos-harrowing-tale-of-captivity-and-courage/ "The Battle for the Soul: Toru Goto’s Harrowing Tale of Captivity and Courage"], ''Bitter Winter'' (August 6, 2025)
author: Massimo Introvigne
textKo: [탈프로그래밍 생존자 토루 고토는] 회복탄력성이 특질이 아니라 선택임을, 신앙은 약함이 아니라 갑옷임을, 자유는 늘 주어지는 것이 아니라 때로는 되찾아야만 하는 것임을 우리에게 가르친다.

text: [C]ourage is reckoned the greatest of all virtues; because, unless a man has that virtue, he has no security for preserving any other.
source: Samuel Johnson, quoted in James Boswell, Life of Samuel Johnson, April 5, 1775 (1791).
sourceRaw: [[Samuel Johnson]], quoted in James Boswell, ''Life of Samuel Johnson'', April 5, 1775 (1791).
author: Samuel Johnson
textKo: 용기는 모든 덕 중에서 가장 위대한 것으로 여겨진다. 사람이 이 덕을 갖지 못하면, 다른 어떤 덕도 지킬 보장이 없기 때문이다.

text: Courage is a quality so necessary for maintaining virtue, that it is always respected, even when it is associated with vice.
source: Samuel Johnson, quoted in James Boswell, Life of Samuel Johnson, June 11, 1784 (1791).
sourceRaw: [[Samuel Johnson]], quoted in James Boswell, ''Life of Samuel Johnson'', June 11, 1784 (1791).
author: Samuel Johnson
textKo: 용기는 덕을 유지하기 위해 너무도 필요한 자질이라, 악과 연결되어 있을 때조차 늘 존경받는다.

text: What really counts is not the immediate act of courage or of valor, but those who bear the struggle day in and day out — not the sunshine patriots but those who are willing to stand for a long period of time.
source: John F. Kennedy, "Remarks at the White House to Members of the American Legion (70)," March 1, 1962, Public Papers of the Presidents: John F. Kennedy, 1962
sourceRaw: [[John F. Kennedy]], [http://www.jfklibrary.org/Research/Research-Aids/Ready-Reference/JFK-Quotations.aspx "Remarks at the White House to Members of the American Legion (70)," March 1, 1962, Public Papers of the Presidents: John F. Kennedy, 1962]
author: John F. Kennedy
textKo: 진정 중요한 것은 즉각적인 용기나 용맹의 행위가 아니라, 날마다 그 분투를 견디는 사람들이다 — 햇볕 좋은 날의 애국자가 아니라, 오랜 시간 굳건히 서 있을 의지가 있는 사람들.

text: Complete courage and absolute cowardice are extremes that very few men fall into. The vast middle space contains all the intermediate kinds and degrees of courage; and these differ as much from one another as men's faces or their humors do.
source: François de La Rochefoucauld, Moral Maxims and Reflections, no. 215 (1665-1678).
sourceRaw: [[François de La Rochefoucauld]], ''Moral Maxims and Reflections'', no. 215 (1665-1678).
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
textKo: 완전한 용기와 절대적 비겁은 극단이라 거의 누구도 거기에 속하지 않는다. 그 광대한 중간 공간이 온갖 종류와 정도의 용기를 담고 있으며, 그것들은 사람들의 얼굴이나 기질만큼이나 서로 다르다.

text: I wanted you to see what real courage is, instead of getting the idea that courage is a man with a gun in his hand. It's when you know you're licked before you begin, but you begin anyway and see it through no matter what.
source: Harper Lee in To Kill a Mockingbird, Part 1, Chapter 11 (1960).
sourceRaw: [[Harper Lee]] in ''[[w:To kill a Mockingbird (novel)|To Kill a Mockingbird]]'', Part 1, Chapter 11 (1960).
author: Harper Lee
textKo: 나는 네가 진짜 용기란 무엇인지 보길 바랐다. 손에 총을 든 사람이 용기라는 생각 대신에 말이다. 그것은 시작도 전에 졌다는 걸 알면서도 어쨌든 시작하고, 무슨 일이 있어도 끝까지 해내는 것이다.

text: [C]ourage is not simply one of the virtues, but the form of every virtue at the testing point, which means, at the point of highest reality. A chastity or honesty, or mercy, which yields to danger will be chaste or honest or merciful only on conditions.
source: C.S. Lewis, The Screwtape Letters (1942), letter XXIX
sourceRaw: [[C.S. Lewis]], ''The Screwtape Letters'' (1942), letter XXIX
author: C.S. Lewis
textKo: 용기는 단지 여러 덕 중 하나가 아니라, 시험의 지점에서 — 곧 최고도의 실재의 지점에서 — 모든 덕이 취하는 형태다. 위험에 굴복하는 정결이나 정직이나 자비는, 조건부의 정결·정직·자비일 뿐이다.

text: This is the art of courage: to see things as they are and still believe that the victory lies not with those who avoid the bad, but those who taste, in living awareness, every drop of the good.
source: Victoria Lincoln, "The Art of Courage," Vogue (October 1, 1952).
sourceRaw: Victoria Lincoln, "The Art of Courage," ''Vogue'' (October 1, 1952).
author: Victoria Lincoln
textKo: 이것이 용기의 기술이다 — 사물을 있는 그대로 보면서도, 승리는 악을 피한 자에게 있는 것이 아니라, 살아 있는 자각으로 선의 모든 한 방울을 맛본 자에게 있다고 여전히 믿는 것.

text: Courage is the ladder on which all the other virtues mount.
source: Clare Boothe Luce, Reader's Digest (May 1979).
sourceRaw: [[Clare Boothe Luce]], ''Reader's Digest'' (May 1979).
author: Clare Boothe Luce
textKo: 용기는 다른 모든 덕이 오르는 사다리다.

text: God grant me the serenityto accept the things I cannot change,courage to change the things I can,and the wisdom to know the difference.
source: Reinhold Niebuhr The Serenity Prayer (c. 1942).
sourceRaw: [[Reinhold Niebuhr]] ''The Serenity Prayer'' (c. 1942).
author: Reinhold Niebuhr
textKo: 신이여, 제가 바꿀 수 없는 것을 받아들이는 평온함을, 바꿀 수 있는 것을 바꾸는 용기를, 그리고 그 둘을 분별하는 지혜를 허락하소서.

text: My courage...exists to catch the future! I'll take my future into my own hands. That's what I wish for! For the courage to keep going forward!
source: Kai Ozu, interpreted by in Mahou Sentai Magiranger (2005), written by , , and Akatsuki Yamatoya
sourceRaw: Kai Ozu, interpreted by {{w|Atsushi Hashimoto}} in ''[[w:Mahou Sentai Magiranger|Mahou Sentai Magiranger]]'' (2005), written by {{w|Jun Maekawa}}, {{w|Naruhisa Arakawa}}, {{w|Michiko Yokote}} and Akatsuki Yamatoya
author: Kai Ozu
textKo: 내 용기는… 미래를 붙잡기 위해 존재한다! 내 미래는 내 손으로 잡겠다. 그것이 내 소원이다! 앞으로 계속 나아갈 용기를!

text: Part of having feelings is learning to integrate them into your life, Data, ...learning to live with them. No matter what the circumstances ... Sometimes it takes courage to try, Data. Courage can be an emotion too.
source: Jean-Luc Picard, Star Trek Generations (1994) story by Brannon Braga, Ronald D. Moore and Rick Berman
sourceRaw: [[Jean-Luc Picard]], ''[[Star Trek Generations|Star Trek Generations]]'' (1994) story by [[w:Brannon Braga|Brannon Braga]], [[w:Ronald D. Moore|Ronald D. Moore]] and [[w:Rick Berman|Rick Berman]]
author: Jean-Luc Picard
textKo: 감정을 갖는다는 것의 일부는, 데이터, 그것을 너의 삶에 통합하는 법, 그것과 함께 사는 법을 배우는 것이다. 어떤 상황에서든… 때로는 시도하는 데에도 용기가 필요하지, 데이터. 용기 역시 감정일 수 있다.

text: You gain strength, courage and confidence by every experience in which you really stop to look fear in the face. You are able to say to yourself, "I lived through this horror. I can take the next thing that comes along." …You must do the thing you think you cannot do.
source: Eleanor Roosevelt, You Learn by Living (1960).
sourceRaw: [[Eleanor Roosevelt]], ''You Learn by Living'' (1960).
author: Eleanor Roosevelt
textKo: 두려움의 얼굴을 정말로 마주하기 위해 멈춰 서는 모든 경험을 통해 너는 힘과 용기와 자신감을 얻는다. 그러면 너는 자신에게 말할 수 있다 — '나는 이 공포를 헤쳐냈다. 다음에 오는 것도 견딜 수 있다.' …너는 네가 할 수 없다고 생각하는 그 일을 반드시 해야 한다.

text: Come one, come all! this rock shall flyFrom its firm base, as soon as I.
source: Walter Scott, Lady of the Lake (1810), Canto V, Stanza 10.
sourceRaw: [[Walter Scott]], ''Lady of the Lake'' (1810), Canto V, Stanza 10.
author: Walter Scott
textKo: 오라, 모두 오라! 이 바위가 그 굳건한 자리에서 떠나는 일이, 내가 자리를 떠나는 일만큼이나 일어나리라.

text: King Richard: A horse! A horse! My kingdom for a horse!Catesby: Withdraw, my lord! I'll help you to a horse.King Richard: Slave, I have set my life upon a cast,And I will stand the hazard of the die.
source: William Shakespeare, Richard III (c. 1591), Act V, scene iv.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Richard III (play)|Richard III]]'' (c. 1591), Act V, scene iv.
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 리처드 왕: 말! 말을 다오! 내 왕국을 말 한 필과 바꾸겠노라! 케이츠비: 물러나소서, 왕이여! 제가 말을 구해드리겠나이다. 리처드 왕: 노예여, 나는 내 목숨을 한 번의 주사위에 걸었다. 운명의 주사위의 위험을 감내하리라.

text: You must not thinkThat we are made of stuff so fat and dullThat we can let our beard be shook with dangerAnd think it pastime.
source: William Shakespeare, Hamlet (1600-02), Act IV, scene 7, line 29.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Hamlet]]'' (1600-02), Act IV, scene 7, line 29.
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 우리가 위험에 수염이 흔들려도 그것을 장난으로 여길 만큼, 그토록 둔하고 무딘 재료로 만들어진 줄 알지는 마라.

text: O, the blood more stirsTo rouse a lion than to start a hare!
source: William Shakespeare, Henry IV, Part I (c. 1597), Act I, scene 3, line 198.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], [[Henry IV, Part 1|''Henry IV'', Part I]] (c. 1597), Act I, scene 3, line 198.
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 오, 토끼를 쫓는 것보다 사자를 깨우는 일에 피가 더 끓는다!

text: The smallest worm will turn being trodden on,And doves will peck in safeguard of their brood.
source: William Shakespeare, Henry VI, Part III (c. 1591), Act II, scene 2, line 17.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], [[Henry VI, Part 3|''Henry VI'', Part III]] (c. 1591), Act II, scene 2, line 17.
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 가장 작은 벌레도 밟히면 몸을 돌리고, 비둘기도 새끼를 지키기 위해 쪼아댄다.

text: Why, courage then! what cannot be avoided'Twere childish weakness to lament or fear.
source: William Shakespeare, Henry VI, Part III (c. 1591), Act V, scene 4, line 37.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], [[Henry VI, Part 3|''Henry VI'', Part III]] (c. 1591), Act V, scene 4, line 37.
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 피할 수 없는 일을 두고 슬퍼하거나 두려워하는 것은 어린아이 같은 약함이다. 그러니, 용기를 내라!

text: Cowards die many times before their deaths;The valiant never taste of death but once.
source: William Shakespeare, Julius Caesar (1599), Act II, scene 2.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Julius Caesar]]'' (1599), Act II, scene 2.
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 겁쟁이는 죽기 전에 여러 번 죽지만, 용감한 자는 단 한 번만 죽음을 맛본다.

text: We fail!But screw your courage to the sticking-place,And we'll not fail.
source: William Shakespeare, Macbeth (1605), Act I, scene 7, line 59.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Macbeth]]'' (1605), Act I, scene 7, line 59.
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 우리가 실패한다고? 다만 너의 용기를 단단히 매어두어라, 그러면 우리는 실패하지 않으리라.

text: I dare do all that may become a man;Who dares do more is none.
source: William Shakespeare, Macbeth (1605), Act I, scene 7.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Macbeth]]'' (1605), Act I, scene 7.
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 사람으로서 마땅한 일이라면 무엇이든 감행하겠다. 그 이상을 감행하는 자는 사람이 아니다.

text: By how much unexpected, by so muchWe must awake endeavour for defence;For courage mounteth with occasion.
source: William Shakespeare, King John (1598), Act II, scene 1, line 80.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[King John]]'' (1598), Act II, scene 1, line 80.
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 예기치 못한 만큼, 우리는 그만큼의 방어를 위한 노력을 깨워야 한다. 용기는 기회와 더불어 솟아오르기 때문이다.

text: Muster your wits: stand in your own defence;Or hide your heads like cowards, and fly hence.
source: William Shakespeare, Love's Labour's Lost (c. 1595-6), Act V, scene 2, line 85.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Love's Labour's Lost]]'' (c. 1595-6), Act V, scene 2, line 85.
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 기지를 모아 자신을 지키든지, 아니면 겁쟁이처럼 머리를 숨기고 여기서 도망쳐라.

text: He hath borne himself beyond the promise of his age, doing, in the figure of a lamb, the feats of a lion.
source: William Shakespeare, Much Ado About Nothing (1598-99), Act I, scene 1, line 13.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Much Ado About Nothing]]'' (1598-99), Act I, scene 1, line 13.
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 그는 자기 나이의 약속을 넘어, 어린양의 모습으로 사자의 위업을 행했다.

text: The thing of courageAs rous'd with rage doth sympathise,And, with an accent tun'd in self-same key,Retorts to chiding fortune.
source: William Shakespeare, Troilus and Cressida (c. 1602), Act I, scene 3, line 51.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Troilus and Cressida]]'' (c. 1602), Act I, scene 3, line 51.
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 용기 있는 것은 분노에 깨어나 공감하며, 자기 자신과 같은 음조로 조율된 어조로, 꾸짖는 운명에 되받아친다.

text: Every great work, every big accomplishment, has been brought into manifestation through holding to the vision, and often just before the big achievement, comes apparent failure and discouragement.
source: Florence Scovel Shinn, from her book The Game of Life (and How to Play it) (1925).
sourceRaw: [[Florence Scovel Shinn]], from her book ''The Game of Life (and How to Play it)'' (1925).
author: Florence Scovel Shinn
textKo: 모든 위대한 업적, 모든 큰 성취는 비전을 붙듦으로써 발현되었으며, 큰 성취 직전에는 흔히 겉으로 보이는 실패와 낙담이 찾아온다.

text: True courage scornsTo vent her prowess in a storm of words;And, to the valiant, actions speak alone.
source: Tobias Smollett, The Regicide (1749), Act II, scene vii.
sourceRaw: [[Tobias Smollett]], ''The Regicide'' (1749), Act II, scene vii.
author: Tobias Smollett
textKo: 진정한 용기는 폭풍 같은 말로 자기 용맹을 뽐내는 것을 경멸한다. 용감한 자에게는 행동만이 말한다.

text: Mental clarity is the child of courage, not the other way around.
source: Nassim Nicholas Taleb, The Bed of Procrustes: Philosophical and Practical Aphorisms (2010) Fooled by Randomness, p.57.
sourceRaw: [[Nassim Nicholas Taleb]], ''The Bed of Procrustes: Philosophical and Practical Aphorisms'' (2010) Fooled by Randomness, p.57.
author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
textKo: 명료한 정신은 용기의 자식이지, 그 반대가 아니다.

text: Who stemm'd the torrent of a downward age.
source: James Thomson, The Seasons, Summer (1727), line 1,516
sourceRaw: [[James Thomson (poet)|James Thomson]], ''The Seasons'', ''Summer'' (1727), line 1,516
author: James Thomson (poet)
textKo: 내려가는 시대의 격류를 막아낸 자.

text: Real courage, however, is shown by those who don’t merely follow the trend or status quo, but who stand up for that which is right and truly just — and don’t kneel.
source: Allen West, "I'd like to see MORE football player protests — NOT less" (27 September 2017)
sourceRaw: [[Allen West (politician)|Allen West]], [https://www.allenbwest.com/2017/09/27/id-like-see-football-player-protests-different-kind/  "I'd like to see MORE football player protests — NOT less"] (27 September 2017)
author: Allen West (politician)
textKo: 그러나 진짜 용기는, 단지 유행이나 현상유지를 따르지 않고, 옳고 진실로 정의로운 것을 위해 일어서고 — 무릎 꿇지 않는 자들이 보여준다.

text: Such is the essence of valor: an unthinking moment, a spark along the spinal nerves, predetermined by the sum total of everything you have ever done, wished to do or not to do, and wish you had done, or hadn't, and then comes the pain.
source: Roger Zelazny, The Moment of the Storm in The Doors of His Face, The Lamps of His Mouth, and Other Stories (1971), p. 199 (originally published in Fantasy & Science Fiction, June 1966)
sourceRaw: [[Roger Zelazny]], ''The Moment of the Storm'' in ''[[w:The Doors of His Face, The Lamps of His Mouth, and Other Stories|The Doors of His Face, The Lamps of His Mouth, and Other Stories]]'' (1971), p. 199 (originally published in ''[[w:The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction|Fantasy & Science Fiction]],'' June 1966)
author: Roger Zelazny
textKo: 그것이 용맹의 본질이다 — 생각 없는 한순간, 척수신경을 따라 번지는 불꽃, 네가 한 일과 하고자 했거나 하지 않으려 했던 일, 했더라면 혹은 하지 말았더라면 하고 바라는 모든 것의 총합에 의해 예정된 것 — 그리고 그 다음에는 아픔이 온다.

text: We are not downhearted, but we cannot understand what is happening to our neighbours.
source: Joseph Chamberlain, speech at Southwick (Jan. 15, 1906).
sourceRaw: [[Joseph Chamberlain]], speech at Southwick (Jan. 15, 1906).
workTitle: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
author: Joseph Chamberlain
sectionPath: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
textKo: 우리는 낙담하지 않았다. 다만 우리 이웃들에게 무슨 일이 일어나고 있는지 이해할 수 없을 뿐이다.

text: The charm of the best courages is that they are inventions, inspirations, flashes of genius.
source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Society and Solitude, Courage.
sourceRaw: [[Ralph Waldo Emerson]], ''Society and Solitude'', Courage.
workTitle: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
sectionPath: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
textKo: 최고의 용기가 지닌 매력은, 그것이 발명이고, 영감이며, 천재의 번뜩임이라는 점에 있다.

text: Be courageous. Be independent. Only remember where the true courage and independence come from.
source: Phillips Brooks, p. 165.
sourceRaw: [[Phillips Brooks]], p. 165.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Phillips Brooks
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 용감하라. 독립적이어라. 다만 진정한 용기와 독립이 어디서 오는지를 기억하라.

text: This is the way to cultivate courage: First, by standing firm on some conscientious principle, some law of duty. Next, by being faithful to truth and right on small occasions and common events. Third, by trusting in God for help and power.
source: James F. Clarke, p. 166.
sourceRaw: [[James F. Clarke]], p. 166.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: James F. Clarke
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 용기를 기르는 길은 이러하다. 첫째, 양심적인 원칙·의무의 법칙 위에 굳건히 서라. 둘째, 작은 기회와 평범한 일들에서도 진리와 정의에 충실하라. 셋째, 도움과 힘을 위해 신을 신뢰하라.

text: Conscience in the soul is the root of all true courage. If a man would be brave, let him learn to obey his conscience.
source: James F. Clarke, p. 167.
sourceRaw: [[James F. Clarke]], p. 167.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: James F. Clarke
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 영혼 속의 양심은 모든 참된 용기의 뿌리다. 용감해지고자 한다면, 자신의 양심에 복종하기를 배우라.

text: A Christian builds his fortitude on a better foundation than stoicism; he is pleased with every thing that happens, because he knows it could not happen unless it first pleased God, and that which pleases Him must be best.
source: Charles Caleb Colton, p. 253.
sourceRaw: [[Charles Caleb Colton]], p. 253.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Charles Caleb Colton
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 그리스도인은 스토아주의보다 더 나은 기초 위에 자신의 굳셈을 세운다. 그는 일어나는 모든 일을 기뻐한다. 그것이 먼저 신을 기쁘게 하지 않았다면 일어날 수 없음을, 그리고 신을 기쁘게 한 것은 반드시 가장 좋은 것임을 알기 때문이다.

text: Consult the honor of religion more, and your personal safety less. Is it for the honor of religion (think you) that Christians should be as timorous as hares to start at every sound?
source: John Flavel, p. 166.
sourceRaw: [[John Flavel]], p. 166.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: John Flavel
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 종교의 명예를 더 깊이 생각하고, 너 자신의 안전은 덜 생각하라. 그리스도인이 작은 소리마다 놀라는 토끼처럼 겁먹어야 종교의 명예가 되겠는가?

text: Bear your burden manfully. Boys at school, young men who have exchanged boyish liberty for serious business, — all who have got a task to do, a work to finish — bear the burden till God gives the signal for repose — till the work is done, and the holiday is fairly earned.
source: James Hamilton, p. 253.
sourceRaw: [[James Hamilton (1814-1871)|James Hamilton]], p. 253.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: James Hamilton (1814-1871)
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 네 짐을 사내답게 짊어지라. 학교의 소년들, 어린 시절의 자유를 진지한 일과 맞바꾼 청년들, 해야 할 일과 끝내야 할 일이 있는 모든 이들은, 신께서 휴식의 신호를 주실 때까지 — 일이 끝나고 휴일이 정당히 얻어질 때까지 — 그 짐을 견디어라.

text: Every man must bear his own burden, and it is a fine thing to see any one trying to do it manfully; carrying his cross bravely, silently, patiently, and in a way which makes you hope that he has taken for his pattern the greatest of all sufferers.
source: James Hamilton, p. 253.
sourceRaw: [[James Hamilton (1814-1871)|James Hamilton]], p. 253.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: James Hamilton (1814-1871)
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 모든 사람은 자기 짐을 져야 한다. 누구든 그것을 사내답게 지려는 것을 — 자신의 십자가를 용감히, 묵묵히, 인내로, 그리고 모든 고난을 가장 크게 견뎌낸 분을 본받았기를 바라게 하는 방식으로 — 보는 것은 아름답다.

text: Gird your hearts with silent fortitude, Suffering, yet hoping all things.
source: Felicia Hemans, p. 253.
sourceRaw: [[Felicia Hemans]], p. 253.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Felicia Hemans
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 고요한 굳셈으로 너의 마음을 두르라 — 고통받으면서도 모든 것을 소망하며.

text: Providence has clearly ordained that the only path fit and salutary for man on earth is the path of persevering fortitude — the unremitting struggle of deliberate self-preparation and humble but active reliance on Divine aid.
source: Elias Lyman Magoon, p. 253.
sourceRaw: [[Elias Lyman Magoon]], p. 253.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Elias Lyman Magoon
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 섭리는 분명히 정해두셨다. 지상에서 인간에게 적합하고 유익한 유일한 길은 끈질긴 굳셈의 길임을 — 곧 의도된 자기 준비의 끊임없는 분투와 신적 도움에 대한 겸손하지만 능동적인 의존.

text: Whenever you do what is holy, be of good cheer, knowing that God Himself takes part with rightful courage.
source: Menander, p. 167.
sourceRaw: [[Menander]], p. 167.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Menander
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 거룩한 일을 행할 때마다, 신께서 친히 의로운 용기를 함께 하심을 알고 기뻐하라.

text: To do an evil action is base; to do a good action without incurring danger is common enough; but it is the part of a good man to do great and noble deeds, though he risks every thing.
source: Plutarch, p. 166.
sourceRaw: [[Plutarch]], p. 166.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Plutarch
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 악한 일을 하는 것은 비루하다. 위험 없이 선을 행하는 것은 흔한 일이다. 그러나 모든 것을 걸고서라도 위대하고 고귀한 일을 행하는 것 — 그것이 선한 사람의 몫이다.

text: My dear friend, venture to take the wind on your face for Christ.
source: Samuel Rutherford, p. 165.
sourceRaw: [[Samuel Rutherford]], p. 165.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Samuel Rutherford
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 내 친구여, 그리스도를 위해 얼굴에 바람을 맞으러 나서기를 감행하라.

text: Be not cast down. If ye saw Him who is standing on the shore, holding out His arms to welcome you to land, ye would wade, not only through a sea of wrongs, but through hell itself to be with Him.
source: Samuel Rutherford, p. 253.
sourceRaw: [[Samuel Rutherford]], p. 253.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Samuel Rutherford
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 낙심하지 말라. 해안에 서서 너를 뭍으로 맞아들이려 팔을 벌리고 계신 그분을 본다면, 너는 잘못의 바다뿐 아니라 지옥 자체라도 헤치고 그분께로 갈 것이다.

text: This nice and subtle happiness of reading, this joy not chilled by age, this polite and unpunished vice, this selfish, serene life-long intoxication.
source: Logan Pearsall Smith — All Trivia (1933) "Afterthoughts" pt. 5
sourceRaw: [[Logan Pearsall Smith]]  — All Trivia (1933) "Afterthoughts" pt. 5
author: Logan Pearsall Smith
textKo: 이 미묘하고 섬세한 독서의 행복이여, 나이에 식지 않는 이 기쁨, 점잖고 벌받지 않는 이 악덕, 이 이기적이고 평온한 평생의 도취여.

text: True happiness is of a retired nature, and an enemy to pomp and noise; it arises, in the first place, from the enjoyment of one's self, and in the next, from the friendship and conversation of a few select companions.
source: Joseph Addison, The Spectator (1711–1714) No. 15 (March 17, 1711)
sourceRaw: [[Joseph Addison]], ''[[w:The Spectator (1711)|The Spectator]]'' (1711–1714) No. 15 (March 17, 1711)
author: Joseph Addison
textKo: 참된 행복은 은둔의 본성을 지니며, 화려함과 소란의 적이다. 그것은 첫째로 자기 자신을 누리는 데서, 다음으로 몇몇 선택된 동반자와의 우정과 대화에서 솟아난다.

text: Happiness was simply something that occurred in a well-regulated life.
source: Brian Aldiss, Steppenpferd, in David G. Hartwell (ed.) Year's Best SF 6, p. 310 (Originally published in Fantasy & Science Fiction magazine, February 2000)
sourceRaw: [[Brian Aldiss]], ''Steppenpferd,'' in [[w:David G. Hartwell|David G. Hartwell]] (ed.) ''[[w:Year's Best SF 6|Year's Best SF 6]],'' p. 310 (Originally published in ''Fantasy & Science Fiction'' magazine, February 2000)
author: Brian Aldiss
textKo: 행복은 단지 잘 정돈된 삶에서 일어나는 어떤 것이었다.

text: The only reality is now, today. What are you waiting for to be happy?...Happiness is not exuberant or noisy, like pleasure or joy; it’s silent, tranquil, and gentle; it’s a feeling of satisfaction inside that begins with self-love.
source: Isabel Allende The Japanese Lover (2015)
sourceRaw: [[Isabel Allende]] The Japanese Lover (2015)
author: Isabel Allende
textKo: 유일한 실재는 지금, 오늘이다. 행복하기 위해 무엇을 기다리는가?… 행복은 쾌락이나 기쁨처럼 들뜨거나 시끄럽지 않다. 그것은 고요하고 평온하고 부드럽다. 자기 사랑에서 시작되는 내면의 만족감이다.

text: To be able without hindrance to exercise his preeminent quality, whatever its nature, is real happiness.
source: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics, X.7, cited in Schopenhauer, Parerga und Paralipomena, E. Payne, trans. (1974) Vol. 1, pp. 341-342
sourceRaw: [[Aristotle]], Nicomachean Ethics, X.7, cited in Schopenhauer, ''Parerga und Paralipomena'', E. Payne, trans. (1974) Vol. 1, pp. 341-342
author: Aristotle
textKo: 방해받지 않고 자신의 탁월한 자질을 — 그것이 무엇이든 — 발휘할 수 있는 것이 진정한 행복이다.

text: Those who do not observe the movements of their own minds must of necessity be unhappy.
source: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations, 2.8
sourceRaw: [[Marcus Aurelius]], ''Meditations'', 2.8
author: Marcus Aurelius
textKo: 자기 마음의 움직임을 관찰하지 않는 자는 반드시 불행해질 수밖에 없다.

text: Happiness is a difficult lesson to learn; it is for mankind a totally new experience and Christ will have to teach men how to handle happiness correctly, to overcome the ancient habits of misery, and thus to know the meaning of true joy. (Chapter 5)
source: Alice Bailey, The Reappearance of the Christ (1947)
sourceRaw: [[Alice Bailey]], ''The Reappearance of the Christ''  (1947)
author: Alice Bailey
textKo: 행복은 배우기 어려운 가르침이다. 그것은 인류에게 완전히 새로운 경험이며, 그리스도는 사람들에게 행복을 올바로 다루는 법을 가르치셔야 할 것이다 — 비참함의 오랜 습관을 극복하고, 참된 기쁨의 의미를 알게 하시려고.

text: I shall take the heart... for brains do not make one happy, and happiness is the best thing in the world.
source: L. Frank Baum, lines for the Tinman in The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900).
sourceRaw: [[L. Frank Baum]], lines for the Tinman in ''[[w:The Wonderful Wizard of Oz|The Wonderful Wizard of Oz]]'' (1900).
author: L. Frank Baum
textKo: 나는 심장을 택하겠다… 두뇌는 사람을 행복하게 해주지 않으니, 행복이야말로 이 세상에서 가장 좋은 것이기 때문이다.

text: In all this world there is nothing so beautiful as a happy child.
source: L. Frank Baum, in lines for Santa Claus in The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus (1902).
sourceRaw: [[L. Frank Baum]], in lines for [[Santa Claus]] in ''The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus'' (1902).
author: L. Frank Baum
textKo: 이 세상에 행복한 아이만큼 아름다운 것은 없다.

text: According to Aristotle, true happiness consists in doing the things we enjoy most with our friends. [...] Those who love philosophy love above all else to philosophise (in Greek: sum-philosophein) with their friends.
source: Enrico Berti, Grazie prof. Berti per aver fatto filosofia insieme a noi!, youtube.com, 19 March 2022 (1:40'-2:58')
sourceRaw: [[Enrico Berti]], ''[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8TdwgdRzxBk Grazie prof. Berti per aver fatto filosofia insieme a noi!]'', ''youtube.com'', 19 March 2022 (1:40'-2:58')
author: Enrico Berti
textKo: 아리스토텔레스에 따르면, 참된 행복은 가장 즐기는 일을 친구들과 함께 하는 데 있다. […] 철학을 사랑하는 자들이 무엇보다도 좋아하는 것은, 친구들과 함께 철학하는 것이다.

text: To have been happy, madame, adds to calamity.
source: Beaumont and Fletcher, The Fair Maid of the Inn (licensed 22 January 1626; 1647), Act I, scene 1, line 250.
sourceRaw: [[Beaumont and Fletcher]], ''The Fair Maid of the Inn'' (licensed 22 January 1626; 1647), Act I, scene 1, line 250.
author: Beaumont and Fletcher
textKo: 행복했었다는 것은, 부인이여, 재앙에 또 하나의 무게를 더할 뿐이외다.

text: HAPPINESS, n. An agreeable sensation arising from contemplating the misery of another.
source: Ambrose Bierce, The Cynic's Dictionary (1906); republished as The Devil's Dictionary (1911).
sourceRaw: [[Ambrose Bierce]], ''The Cynic's Dictionary'' (1906); republished as ''The Devil's Dictionary'' (1911).
author: Ambrose Bierce
textKo: 행복, 명사. 다른 이의 비참함을 응시하는 데서 일어나는 유쾌한 감각.

text: Ah! The happy ones of this world who are assured their daily bread—that is, all the things necessary to bodily life—and who, not wishing to know Jesus, have never for one single instant had the idea of suffering for their brothers, of sacrificing themselves for the wretched!
source: Léon Bloy, Pilgrim of the Absolute (1947), p. 2
sourceRaw: [[Léon Bloy]], ''Pilgrim of the Absolute'' (1947), p. 2
author: Léon Bloy
textKo: 아! 이 세상의 행복한 자들 — 매일의 빵, 곧 육체의 삶에 필요한 모든 것을 보장받고, 예수를 알기를 원치 않으며, 형제들을 위해 고난받고 가련한 자들을 위해 자신을 희생할 생각을 단 한순간도 해본 적 없는 자들이여!

text: Do not fall prey to seeking pure happiness. Instead, seek lifelong progress toward happierness.
source: Arthur C. Brooks, "Jung’s Five Pillars of a Good Life," The Atlantic, 2024
sourceRaw: Arthur C. Brooks, "Jung’s Five Pillars of a Good Life," ''The Atlantic'', 2024
author: Arthur C. Brooks
textKo: 순수한 행복을 좇는 함정에 빠지지 마라. 그 대신 '더 행복해짐'을 향한 평생의 진전을 추구하라.

text: Happiness lies only in a divine unrest; and if you are lapped in comfort you stagnate and miss it.
source: John Buchan, A Lodge in the Wilderness (1906), Chapter I.
sourceRaw: [[John Buchan, 1st Baron Tweedsmuir|John Buchan]], ''A Lodge in the Wilderness'' (1906), Chapter I.
author: John Buchan, 1st Baron Tweedsmuir
textKo: 행복은 오직 신성한 불안 속에 있다. 안락에 파묻혀 있다면 너는 정체하고 그것을 놓치게 된다.

text: Happy indeed we live, free from avarice amidst the avaricious. Amidst the avaricious men we dwell free from avarice.Happy indeed we live, we who possess nothing. Feeders on joy we shall be, like the Radiant Gods.Victory begets enmity; the defeated dwell in pain. Happily the peaceful live, discarding both victory and defeat.
source: Gautama Buddha, Dhammapada, 199-201
sourceRaw: [[Gautama Buddha]], Dhammapada, 199-201
author: Gautama Buddha
textKo: 우리는 진정 행복하게 산다 — 탐욕스러운 자들 가운데 탐욕 없이. 탐욕스러운 자들 가운데 우리는 탐욕 없이 거한다. 우리는 진정 행복하게 산다 — 아무것도 소유하지 않은 우리는. 빛나는 신들처럼 기쁨을 먹고 살아가리라. 승리는 적의를 낳고, 패한 자는 고통 속에 거한다. 승리와 패배를 모두 버린 자, 평화로운 자들이 행복하게 산다.

text: The achievement of happiness requires not the ... satisfaction of our needs ... but the examination and transformation of those needs.
source: Stanley Cavell, Pursuits of Happiness (1984)
sourceRaw: [[Stanley Cavell]], ''Pursuits of Happiness'' (1984)
author: Stanley Cavell
textKo: 행복의 성취가 요구하는 것은… 우리의 욕구를 충족시키는 것이 아니라, 그 욕구들을 검토하고 변형하는 것이다.

text: The soul of the world is nourished by people's happiness.
source: Paulo Coelho, The Alchemist (1988) The Old King, p. 22.
sourceRaw: [[Paulo Coelho]],  ''The Alchemist'' (1988)  The Old King, p. 22.
author: Paulo Coelho
textKo: 세상의 영혼은 사람들의 행복으로 양분을 얻는다.

text: Stay close to those who sing, tell stories, enjoy life and whose eyes sparkle with happiness. Because happiness is contagious and will always manage to find a solution whereas logic can find only an explanation for the mistake made.
source: Paulo Coelho, Manuscript Found in Accra (2012)
sourceRaw: [[Paulo Coelho]],  ''[[Manuscript Found in Accra]]''  (2012)
author: Paulo Coelho
textKo: 노래하고 이야기를 나누며 삶을 즐기는, 눈이 행복으로 반짝이는 사람들 곁에 머물러라. 행복은 전염되며 늘 해결책을 찾아내지만, 논리는 저질러진 실수에 대한 설명만 찾을 뿐이다.

text: Happiness lies in the fulfillment of the spirit through the body.
source: Cyril Connolly, The Unquiet Grave (1945), Part I.
sourceRaw: [[Cyril Connolly]], ''The Unquiet Grave'' (1945), Part I.
author: Cyril Connolly
textKo: 행복은 육체를 통한 정신의 충만에 있다.

text: Domestic Happiness, thou only blissOf Paradise that hast survived the Fall!
source: William Cowper, The Task (1785), Book III, line 41.
sourceRaw: [[William Cowper]], ''The Task'' (1785), Book III, line 41.
author: William Cowper
textKo: 가정의 행복이여, 너만이 타락에서 살아남은 낙원의 유일한 축복이로다!

text: Thus happiness depends, as Nature shows,Less on exterior things than most suppose.
source: William Cowper in Table Talk (1817) line 246.
sourceRaw: [[William Cowper]] in ''Table Talk'' (1817) line 246.
author: William Cowper
textKo: 그러므로 자연이 보여주듯, 행복은 대부분이 짐작하는 것보다 외부의 것에 덜 의존한다.

text: It is not the smallest use to try to make people good, unless you try at the same time — and they feel that you are trying — to make them happy. And you rarely can make another happy, unless you are happy yourself.
source: Dinah Craik, A Woman's Thoughts About Women (1858), Ch. 10.
sourceRaw: [[Dinah Craik]], ''A Woman's Thoughts About Women'' (1858), Ch. 10.
author: Dinah Craik
textKo: 동시에 사람들을 행복하게 하려고 — 그리고 사람들이 너의 그 노력을 느끼게 — 하지 않으면, 사람들을 선하게 만들려는 시도는 아무 소용이 없다. 그리고 자신이 행복하지 않은 한, 너는 좀처럼 남을 행복하게 할 수 없다.

text: Happiness! Can any human being undertake to define it for another?
source: Dinah Craik, A Woman's Thoughts About Women (1858), Ch. 10.
sourceRaw: [[Dinah Craik]], ''A Woman's Thoughts About Women'' (1858), Ch. 10.
author: Dinah Craik
textKo: 행복! 어떤 인간이 그것을 다른 인간에게 정의해줄 수 있겠는가?

text: The only way to make people good, is to make them happy.
source: Dinah Craik, A Woman's Thoughts About Women (1858), Ch. 11.
sourceRaw: [[Dinah Craik]], ''A Woman's Thoughts About Women'' (1858), Ch. 11.
author: Dinah Craik
textKo: 사람을 선하게 만드는 유일한 길은, 그들을 행복하게 하는 것이다.

text: The lower animals, like man, manifestly feel pleasure and pain, happiness and misery. Happiness is never better exhibited than by young animals, such as puppies, kittens, lambs, &c., when playing together, like our own children.
source: Charles Darwin, The Descent of Man (1871), volume I, chapter III: "Comparison of the Mental Powers of Man and the Lower Animals — continued", p. 39.
sourceRaw: [[Charles Darwin]], ''[[w:The Descent of Man, and Selection in Relation to Sex|The Descent of Man]]'' (1871), volume I, chapter III: "Comparison of the Mental Powers of Man and the Lower Animals — continued", [http://darwin-online.org.uk/content/frameset?pageseq=52&itemID=F937.1&viewtype=image p. 39].
author: Charles Darwin
textKo: 하등 동물들도 인간처럼 쾌락과 고통, 행복과 비참을 분명히 느낀다. 행복이 가장 잘 드러나는 것은, 강아지·새끼고양이·새끼양 같은 어린 동물들이 우리 아이들처럼 함께 노는 모습에서다.

text: We can't be happy or healthy if we don't take care of our life support system, the planet.
source: Sylvia Earle Interview with NPR (2021)
sourceRaw: [[Sylvia Earle]] [https://www.npr.org/transcripts/1009952391 Interview] with NPR (2021)
author: Sylvia Earle
textKo: 우리의 생명 지원 체계인 이 행성을 돌보지 않으면, 우리는 행복할 수도 건강할 수도 없다.

text: Happiness in the ordinary sense is not what one needs in life, though one is right to aim at it. The true satisfaction is to come through and see those whom one loves come through.
source: E. M. Forster, Selected Letters: Letter 216, to Florence Barger, 11 February 1922.
sourceRaw: [[E. M. Forster]], ''Selected Letters'': Letter 216, to Florence Barger, 11 February 1922.
author: E. M. Forster
textKo: 평범한 의미의 행복이 삶에서 우리에게 필요한 것은 아니다. 비록 그것을 목표로 삼는 것이 옳더라도. 진정한 만족은 자신이 살아남고, 사랑하는 이들이 살아남는 것을 보는 것이다.

text: Happiness is when what you think, what you say, and what you do are in harmony.
source: Mahatma Gandhi, as quoted in Humor, Play, & Laughter : Stress-proofing Life with Your Kids (1998) by Joseph A. Michelli, p. 88.
sourceRaw: [[Mahatma Gandhi]], as quoted in ''Humor, Play, & Laughter : Stress-proofing Life with Your Kids'' (1998) by Joseph A. Michelli, p. 88.
author: Mahatma Gandhi
textKo: 행복이란 네가 생각하는 것, 말하는 것, 행하는 것이 조화를 이룰 때다.

text: We call “happiness” a certain set of circumstances that makes joy possible. But we call joy that state of mind and emotions that needs nothing to feel happy.
source: André Gide, “An Unprejudiced Mind,” Pretexts, J. O’Brien, ed. (1964) p. 326
sourceRaw: [[André Gide]], “An Unprejudiced Mind,” ''Pretexts'', J. O’Brien, ed. (1964) p. 326
author: André Gide
textKo: 우리는 기쁨을 가능하게 하는 어떤 일련의 상황을 '행복'이라 부른다. 그러나 행복하기 위해 아무것도 필요로 하지 않는 그 마음과 감정의 상태를 우리는 '기쁨'이라 부른다.

text: Still to ourselves in every place consign'd,Our own felicity to make or find.
source: Oliver Goldsmith, The Traveller (1764), line 431.
sourceRaw: [[Oliver Goldsmith]], ''The Traveller'' (1764), line 431.
author: Oliver Goldsmith
textKo: 여전히 우리 자신은 어디에 있든 우리에게 맡겨져 있다 — 자신의 행복을 스스로 만들거나 찾는 것.

text: It is the law of life that if you are kind to someone you feel happy. If you are cruel you are unhappy.
source: Cary Grant, as quoted in "Love – That’s All Cary Grant Ever Thinks About" by Sheilah Graham Westbrook in Motion Picture (June 1964).
sourceRaw: [[Cary Grant]], as quoted in [http://www.carygrant.net/articles/thinks%20about.htm "Love – That’s All Cary Grant Ever Thinks About"] by  [[w:Sheilah Graham Westbrook|Sheilah Graham Westbrook]] in ''Motion Picture'' (June 1964).
author: Cary Grant
textKo: 누군가에게 친절하면 행복해지고, 잔인하면 불행해진다 — 그것이 삶의 법칙이다.

text: For 2500 years, Buddhists have systematically studied the essence and cause of happiness. which is why there is a growing interest among the scientific community both in their philosophy and their meditation practices.
source: Yuval Noah Harari, Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind (2011), Chapter 19: "And they lived happily Ever After"
sourceRaw: [[Yuval Noah Harari]], Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind (2011), Chapter 19: "And they lived happily Ever After"
author: Yuval Noah Harari
textKo: 2500년 동안 불교도들은 행복의 본질과 원인을 체계적으로 연구해왔다. 그래서 그들의 철학과 명상 수행에 대해 과학계의 관심이 커지고 있다.

text: Scholars began to study the history of happiness only a few years ago, and we are still formulating initial hypotheses and searching for appropriate research methods.
source: Yuval Noah Harari, Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind (2011), Chapter 19: "And they lived happily Ever After"
sourceRaw: [[Yuval Noah Harari]], Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind (2011), Chapter 19: "And they lived happily Ever After"
author: Yuval Noah Harari
textKo: 학자들이 행복의 역사를 연구하기 시작한 것은 불과 몇 년 전이며, 우리는 아직 초기 가설을 세우고 적절한 연구 방법을 찾는 중이다.

text: Freud's prescription for personal happiness as consisting of work and love must be taken with the proviso that the work has to be loved, and the love has to be worked at.
source: Sydney J. Harris, Pieces of Eight (1982).
sourceRaw: [[Sydney J. Harris]], ''Pieces of Eight'' (1982).
author: Sydney J. Harris
textKo: 개인의 행복이 일과 사랑에 있다는 프로이트의 처방은 한 가지 단서를 붙여야 한다 — 일은 사랑받아야 하고, 사랑은 일하듯 노력해야 한다는 것.

text: Happiness in this world, when it comes, comes incidentally. Make it the object of pursuit, and it leads us a wild-goose chase, and is never attained. Follow some other object, and very possibly we may find that we have caught happiness without dreaming of it.
source: Nathaniel Hawthorne in The American Notebooks (1851).
sourceRaw: [[Nathaniel Hawthorne]] in ''The American Notebooks'' (1851).
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
textKo: 이 세상의 행복은, 올 때면 우연히 부수적으로 온다. 그것을 추구의 대상으로 삼으면 헛수고에 끌려다닐 뿐 결코 얻지 못한다. 다른 목표를 좇다 보면, 꿈에도 모른 채 행복을 붙들었음을 발견할지도 모른다.

text: Happiness is not achieved by the conscious pursuit of happiness; it is generally the by-product of other activities.
source: Aldous Huxley, Essay "Distractions I" in Vedanta for the Western World (1945) edited by Christopher Isherwood
sourceRaw: [[Aldous Huxley]], Essay "Distractions I" in ''Vedanta for the Western World'' (1945) edited by [[Christopher Isherwood]]
author: Aldous Huxley
textKo: 행복은 의식적인 행복의 추구로 얻어지지 않는다. 그것은 보통 다른 활동의 부산물이다.

text: I'd rather be unhappy than have the sort of false, lying happiness you were having here.
source: Aldous Huxley, John in Brave New World (1932), ch. 12
sourceRaw: [[Aldous Huxley]], John in ''Brave New World'' (1932), ch. 12
author: Aldous Huxley
textKo: 여기서 네가 누리던 그 거짓되고 가식적인 행복보다는, 차라리 나는 불행한 편이 낫다.

text: Our Ford himself did a great deal to shift the emphasis from truth and beauty to comfort and happiness. Mass production demanded the shift. Universal happiness keeps the wheels steadily turning; truth and beauty can't.
source: Aldous Huxley, Mustapha Mond in Brave New World (1932), ch. 16
sourceRaw: [[Aldous Huxley]], Mustapha Mond in ''Brave New World'' (1932), ch. 16
author: Aldous Huxley
textKo: 우리의 포드는 진리와 아름다움에서 안락과 행복으로 강조점을 옮기는 데 큰 역할을 했다. 대량 생산이 그 전환을 요구했다. 보편적 행복은 톱니바퀴를 꾸준히 돌리지만, 진리와 아름다움은 그러지 못한다.

text: The happiest people seem to be those who have no particular cause for being happy except that they are so.
source: William Ralph Inge como citado in: The Reader's Digest - Volume 123 - Página 79, Reader's Digest Association, 1983
sourceRaw: [[William Ralph Inge]] como citado in: The Reader's Digest - Volume 123 - Página 79, Reader's Digest Association, 1983
author: William Ralph Inge
textKo: 가장 행복한 사람들은 행복할 특별한 이유가 없는 사람들 — 그저 그렇게 행복한 사람들인 것 같다.

text: Reason, Observation and Experience — the Holy Trinity of Science — have taught us that happiness is the only good; that the time to be happy is now, and the way to be happy is to make others so.
source: Robert G. Ingersoll, "The Gods" (1876) as published in The Gods and Other Lectures (1879).
sourceRaw: [[Robert G. Ingersoll]], "The Gods" (1876) as published in T''he Gods and Other Lectures'' (1879).
author: Robert G. Ingersoll
textKo: 이성·관찰·경험 — 과학의 성삼위 — 은 우리에게 가르쳤다. 행복만이 유일한 선이며, 행복할 때는 지금이고, 행복하는 방법은 남을 행복하게 하는 것이라고.

text: Perfect happiness I believe was never intended by the deity to be the lot of any one of his creatures in this world; but that he has very much put in our power the nearness of our approaches to it, is what I as stedfastly believe.
source: Thomas Jefferson, letter to John Page (July 15, 1763); in Julian P. Boyd, ed., The Papers of Thomas Jefferson (1950), vol. 1, p. 10. Jefferson used the spelling "beleive". This letter was written in hopes that John Page would talk to Belinda, a young woman with whom Jefferson, then 20, was infatuated. Jefferson was normally cool and level-headed, but Belinda had a devastating effect on his poise, leaving him tongue-tied and stammering. Saul K. Padover, Jefferson (1942), chapter 2, p. 20.
sourceRaw: [[Thomas Jefferson]], letter to John Page (July 15, 1763); in Julian P. Boyd, ed., ''The Papers of Thomas Jefferson'' (1950), vol. 1, p. 10. Jefferson used the spelling "beleive". This letter was written in hopes that John Page would talk to Belinda, a young woman with whom Jefferson, then 20, was infatuated. Jefferson was normally cool and level-headed, but Belinda had a devastating effect on his poise, leaving him tongue-tied and stammering. Saul K. Padover, ''Jefferson'' (1942), chapter 2, p. 20.
author: Thomas Jefferson
textKo: 이 세상에서 어느 누구에게도 완전한 행복이 신의 뜻이 아니었다고 나는 믿는다. 그러나 그 행복에 얼마나 가까이 다가갈 수 있는지는 그분이 우리에게 크게 맡기셨다고, 나는 그만큼 굳건히 믿는다.

text: We hold these truths to be sacred and undeniable; that and independent, that from that equal creation they derive rights inherent and inalienable, among which are the preservation of .
source: Thomas Jefferson early draft for the Declaration of Independence (June 1776).
sourceRaw: [[Thomas Jefferson]] early draft for the [[w:Declaration_of_Independence_%28United_States%29|Declaration of Independence]] (June 1776).
author: Thomas Jefferson
textKo: 우리는 다음 진리들이 신성하고 부인할 수 없는 것임을 견지한다. 모든 사람은 평등하게 창조되었으며, 그 평등한 창조로부터 양도할 수 없는 천부의 권리들을 부여받았으니, 그중에 생명의 보전이 있다.

text: The happiest moments of my life have been the few which I have past at home in the bosom of my family…. public emploiment contributes neither to advantage nor happiness. It is but honorable exile from one's family and affairs.
source: Thomas Jefferson, secretary of state, letter to Francis Willis, Jr. (April 18, 1790); in Julian P. Boyd, ed., The Papers of Thomas Jefferson (1961), vol. 16, p. 353. Willis served in Congress 1791–1793.
sourceRaw: [[Thomas Jefferson]], secretary of state, letter to Francis Willis, Jr. (April 18, 1790); in Julian P. Boyd, ed., ''The Papers of Thomas Jefferson'' (1961), vol. 16, p. 353. Willis served in Congress 1791–1793.
author: Thomas Jefferson
textKo: 내 인생에서 가장 행복한 순간들은 가족의 품 안 집에서 보낸 몇 안 되는 시간들이었다… 공직은 이로움도 행복도 가져다주지 않는다. 그것은 다만 자신의 가족과 일로부터의 명예로운 유배일 뿐이다.

text: The care of human life and happiness, and not their destruction, is the first and only legitimate object of good government.
source: Thomas Jefferson Letter "to the Republican Citizens of Washington County, Maryland" (31 March 1809).
sourceRaw: [[Thomas Jefferson]] Letter "to the Republican Citizens of Washington County, Maryland" (31 March 1809).
author: Thomas Jefferson
textKo: 인간의 생명과 행복을 돌보는 것 — 그것을 파괴하는 것이 아니라 — 이 좋은 정부의 첫째이자 유일한 정당한 목적이다.

text: Only when the happiness is past and we look back on it we do suddenly realize — sometimes with astonishment — how happy we had been.
source: Nikos Kazantzakis, Zorba the Greek (1946), Ch. 6.
sourceRaw: [[Nikos Kazantzakis]], ''[[Zorba the Greek]]'' (1946), Ch. 6.
author: Nikos Kazantzakis
textKo: 행복은 지나간 뒤 돌아볼 때에야 우리는 갑자기 — 때로는 놀라움 속에 — 우리가 얼마나 행복했었는지 깨닫는다.

text: How simple and frugal a thing is happiness: a glass of wine, a roast chestnut, a wretched little brazier, the sound of the sea. … All that is required to feel that here and now is happiness is a simple, frugal heart.
source: Nikos Kazantzakis, Zorba the Greek (1946), Ch. 7.
sourceRaw: [[Nikos Kazantzakis]], ''[[Zorba the Greek]]'' (1946), Ch. 7.
author: Nikos Kazantzakis
textKo: 행복은 얼마나 단순하고 검소한가 — 한 잔의 포도주, 구운 밤 한 알, 보잘것없는 작은 화로, 바다의 소리… 지금 여기가 곧 행복임을 느끼는 데 필요한 것은 단순하고 검소한 마음 하나뿐이다.

text: Once more I realized to what an extent earthly happiness is made to the measure of man. It is not a rare bird which we must pursue at one moment in heaven, at the next in our minds. Happiness is a domestic bird found in our own courtyards.
source: Nikos Kazantzakis, The Last Temptation of Christ (1951), Ch. 10.
sourceRaw: [[Nikos Kazantzakis]], ''[[w:The Last Temptation of Christ|The Last Temptation of Christ]]'' (1951), Ch. 10.
author: Nikos Kazantzakis
textKo: 다시 한번 나는 깨달았다. 지상의 행복은 인간의 치수에 맞게 만들어져 있다는 것을. 그것은 어느 순간엔 하늘에서, 다음 순간엔 마음속에서 좇아야 하는 희귀한 새가 아니다. 행복은 우리 자신의 마당에서 발견되는 집새다.

text: The great happiness-secret, after all, is division. How dare we, in this vain, fleeting world, concentrate our whole freight of interest in one frail bark ?
source: Letitia Elizabeth Landon, Romance and Reality (1831), Vol. III, chapter 9
sourceRaw: [[Letitia Elizabeth Landon]], ''[[Romance and Reality]]'' (1831), Vol. III, chapter 9
author: Letitia Elizabeth Landon
textKo: 행복의 큰 비밀은 결국 분산이다. 이 허망하고 덧없는 세상에서, 어찌 우리의 모든 관심의 짐을 하나의 연약한 배에 다 실어 보낼 수 있겠는가?

text: To use the established phrase, three months of uninterrupted happiness glided away—a phrase, though in frequent use, whose accuracy I greatly doubt ; there being no such thing as uninterrupted happiness any how or any where.
source: Letitia Elizabeth Landon, Heath's Book of Beauty, 1833 (1832), 'The Talisman'
sourceRaw: [[Letitia Elizabeth Landon]], ''Heath's Book of Beauty, 1833'' (1832), 'The Talisman'
author: Letitia Elizabeth Landon
textKo: 흔히 쓰이는 표현으로, '중단 없는 행복의 세 달이 흘러갔다' — 자주 쓰이지만 그 정확성을 나는 크게 의심한다. 어디에서도 어떤 식으로도 '중단 없는 행복'이라는 것은 존재하지 않으므로.

text: And yet it is a wasted heart :It is a wasted mindThat seeks not in the inner worldIts happiness to find ;For happiness is like the birdThat broods above its nest,And finds beneath its folded wings,Life's dearest, and its best.
source: Letitia Elizabeth Landon, Ethel Churchill (or The Two Brides) (1837), Vol. III, Chapter 1
sourceRaw: [[Letitia Elizabeth Landon]], ''[[Ethel Churchill (or The Two Brides)]]'' (1837), Vol. III, Chapter 1
author: Letitia Elizabeth Landon
textKo: 그러나 내면의 세계에서 행복을 찾지 않는 마음은 낭비된 마음이다. 행복이란 둥지 위에 품고 앉은 새와 같아서, 그 접힌 날개 아래에서 삶의 가장 소중하고 가장 좋은 것을 발견하기 때문이다.

text: If a man lives under the delusion that he can do anything that he likes, and that the effect of his actions will never recoil upon himself, he will most certainly find that some of these actions eventually involve him in unhappiness and suffering.
source: C.W. Leadbeater, (Speaking about the Four Noble Truths in The Masters and the Path, (1925)
sourceRaw: [[C.W. Leadbeater]], (Speaking about the [[Four Noble Truths]] in ''The Masters and the Path'', (1925)
author: C.W. Leadbeater
textKo: 자신이 원하는 것은 무엇이든 할 수 있고, 그 행동의 결과가 결코 자신에게 되돌아오지 않을 것이라는 망상 속에 사는 자는, 머지않아 그중 일부 행동이 자신을 불행과 고통으로 끌어들임을 분명히 알게 될 것이다.

text: We meet this evening, not in sorrow, but in gladness of heart.
source: Abraham Lincoln, last public address (April 11, 1865); in Roy P. Basler, ed., The Collected Works of Abraham Lincoln, vol. 8, p. 399 (1953). On April 9, Lee had surrendered.
sourceRaw: [[Abraham Lincoln]], last public address (April 11, 1865); in Roy P. Basler, ed., ''The Collected Works of Abraham Lincoln'', vol. 8, p. 399 (1953). On April 9, Lee had surrendered.
author: Abraham Lincoln
textKo: 오늘 저녁 우리는 슬픔이 아니라 마음의 기쁨으로 모였습니다.

text: The rays of happiness, like those of light, are colorless when unbroken.
source: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, Kavanagh: A Tale (1849), Chapter XIII.
sourceRaw: [[Henry Wadsworth Longfellow]], ''Kavanagh: A Tale'' (1849), Chapter XIII.
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
textKo: 행복의 광선은 빛의 광선과 같이, 분산되지 않을 때엔 색이 없다.

text: Happiness exists on earth, and it is won through prudent exercise of reason, knowledge of the harmony of the universe, and constant practice of generosity.
source: José Martí, My Race (1893), "Mi Raza", first published in Patria (16 April 1893) Full translation online.
sourceRaw: [[José Martí]], My Race (1893), "Mi Raza", first published in ''Patria'' (16 April 1893) [http://www.historyofcuba.com/history/race/MyRace.htm Full translation online].
author: José Martí
textKo: 행복은 지상에 존재한다. 그것은 이성의 신중한 행사, 우주의 조화에 대한 앎, 그리고 끊임없는 너그러움의 실천으로 얻어진다.

text: Tolerant people are the happiest, so why not get rid of prejudices that hold you back?
source: William Moulton Marston 1939 Your Life What are your prejudices?
sourceRaw: [[William Moulton Marston]] 1939 ''Your Life'' ''What are your prejudices?''
author: William Moulton Marston
textKo: 관용적인 사람이 가장 행복하다. 그렇다면 왜 너를 붙드는 편견들을 떨쳐버리지 않는가?

text: People often don't appreciate how complex happiness may be. They think happy people are shallow, which can be so wrong. It's actually far easier to be unhappy than it is to be happy. It requires more effort, more understanding, more character to be consistently happy.
source: Alexander McCall Smith, The Sweet Remnants of Summer (2022), chapter 4
sourceRaw: [[Alexander McCall Smith]], ''The Sweet Remnants of Summer'' (2022), chapter 4
author: Alexander McCall Smith
textKo: 사람들은 흔히 행복이 얼마나 복잡할 수 있는지 잘 모른다. 행복한 사람들이 얄팍하다고 여기지만, 그건 큰 오해다. 사실 행복한 것보다 불행한 것이 훨씬 쉽다. 일관되게 행복하려면 더 많은 노력, 더 많은 이해, 더 강한 인격이 필요하다.

text: In every life we have some trouble, but when you worry? You make it double. Don't worry, be happy.
source: Bobby McFerrin, Simple Pleasures, (album) Don't Worry, Be Happy 2008, (single)
sourceRaw: Bobby McFerrin, ''[[w:Simple Pleasures (Bobby McFerrin album)|Simple Pleasures]]'', (album) ''Don't Worry, Be Happy'' 2008,  (single)
author: Bobby McFerrin
textKo: 누구나 살면서 어려움이 있지만, 걱정한다고? 그러면 그 걱정이 두 배가 될 뿐이야. 걱정하지 말고, 행복해라.

text: Happiness is surely the best teacher of good manners: only the unhappy are churlish in deportment.
source: Christopher Morley, Where the Blue Begins (1922).
sourceRaw: [[Christopher Morley]], ''Where the Blue Begins'' (1922).
author: Christopher Morley
textKo: 행복이야말로 좋은 예절의 가장 훌륭한 스승이다. 무례하게 구는 사람은 오직 불행한 사람뿐이다.

text: The rich philistinism emanating from advertisements is due not to their exaggerating (or inventing) the glory of this or that serviceable article but to suggesting that the acme of human happiness is purchasable and that its purchase somehow ennobles the purchaser.
source: Vladimir Nabokov, “Philistines and Philistinism,” Lectures on Russian Literature (1981)
sourceRaw: [[Vladimir Nabokov]], “Philistines and Philistinism,” ''Lectures on Russian Literature'' (1981)
author: Vladimir Nabokov
textKo: 광고에서 풍기는 부유한 속물성은, 어떤 유용한 물건의 영광을 과장하거나 지어내기 때문이 아니라, 인간 행복의 정점이 구매 가능한 것이며 그 구매가 어떻게든 구매자를 고귀하게 만든다고 암시하기 때문에 생긴다.

text: What is happiness? The feeling that power is growing, that resistance is overcome.
source: Friedrich Nietzsche, The Antichrist (1888), sec. 2.
sourceRaw: [[Friedrich Nietzsche]], ''[[w:The Antichrist (book)|The Antichrist]]'' (1888), sec. 2.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
textKo: 행복이란 무엇인가? 힘이 자라고 있다는 느낌, 저항이 극복되고 있다는 느낌이다.

text: For happiness, she also required work to do in this world and bread on the table.
source: Grace Paley "Midrash on Happiness" (1990)
sourceRaw: [[Grace Paley]]  "Midrash on Happiness" (1990)
author: Grace Paley
textKo: 행복하기 위해서, 그녀에게는 또한 이 세상에서 할 일과 식탁 위의 빵이 필요했다.

text: Oh happiness! our being's end and aim!Good, Pleasure, Ease, Content! whate'er thy name;That something still which prompts th' eternal sigh,For which we bear to live, or dare to die.
source: Alexander Pope, An Essay on Man (1733-34), Epistle IV, line 1.
sourceRaw: [[Alexander Pope]], ''An Essay on Man'' (1733-34), Epistle IV, line 1.
author: Alexander Pope
textKo: 오 행복이여! 우리 존재의 끝이자 목적이여! 선, 쾌락, 안락, 만족 — 그 어떤 이름이든; 영원한 한숨을 자아내고, 그것을 위해 우리가 살기를 참거나 죽음을 감히 마주하는, 바로 그것이여.

text: Fix'd to no spot is Happiness sincere;'Tis nowhere to be found, or ev'rywhere;'Tis never to be bought, but always free.
source: Alexander Pope, An Essay on Man (1733-34), Epistle IV, line 15.
sourceRaw: [[Alexander Pope]], ''An Essay on Man'' (1733-34), Epistle IV, line 15.
author: Alexander Pope
textKo: 참된 행복은 어느 한 자리에 매여 있지 않다. 그것은 어디에도 없거나, 어디에나 있다. 살 수 있는 것이 아니라, 늘 자유로이 주어지는 것이다.

text: Heaven to mankind impartial we confess,If all are equal in their happiness;But mutual wants this happiness increase,All nature's difference keeps all nature's peace.
source: Alexander Pope, An Essay on Man (1733-34), Epistle IV, line 53.
sourceRaw: [[Alexander Pope]], ''An Essay on Man'' (1733-34), Epistle IV, line 53.
author: Alexander Pope
textKo: 우리는 인정하노라, 모두가 행복에 있어 평등하다면 하늘은 인류에게 공평한 것을. 그러나 서로의 필요가 이 행복을 늘리고, 자연의 모든 차이가 자연의 평화를 지킨다.

text: Happiness is a battle to be waged and not a feeling to be awaited.
source: Dennis Prager, Happiness is a Serious Problem (1998), p. 5
sourceRaw: [[Dennis Prager]], ''Happiness is a Serious Problem'' (1998), p. 5
author: Dennis Prager
textKo: 행복은 기다려야 할 감정이 아니라, 싸워서 얻어야 할 전투다.

text: Perfect the Will, the Mind, Feeling, their corporeal organs and their material tools; be useful to yourselves, to your own ones, and to others; and Happiness, insofar as it exists on this earth, will come of itself."
source: Bolesław Prus, The Most General Life Ideals, 2nd, revised edition, Warsaw, 1905. (Newspaper serialization, 1897–99; 1st book edition, 1901).
sourceRaw: [[Bolesław Prus]], ''[[Wikisource:The Most General Life Ideals|The Most General Life Ideals]]'', 2nd, revised edition, Warsaw, 1905. (Newspaper serialization, 1897–99; 1st book edition, 1901).
author: Bolesław Prus
textKo: 의지·정신·감정과 그 육체적 기관과 물질적 도구를 완성하라. 너 자신과 너의 사람들과 다른 이들에게 유익한 자가 되라. 그러면 이 지상에 존재하는 한, 행복은 저절로 찾아올 것이다.

text: The key to self-generated happiness (the only reliable kind) is the refusal to take oneself too seriously.
source: Tom Robbins, in "The Green Man : Tom Robbins" interviewed by Gregory Daurer, in High Times (12 June 2002).
sourceRaw: [[Tom Robbins]], in [http://www.hightimes.com/read/green-man-tom-robbins "The Green Man : Tom Robbins" interviewed by Gregory Daurer, in ''High Times'' (12 June 2002)].
author: Tom Robbins
textKo: 스스로 만들어내는 행복(유일하게 믿을 만한 행복)의 열쇠는 자신을 너무 진지하게 받아들이지 않는 것이다.

text: Happiness is the only sanction of life; where happiness fails, existence remains a mad and lamentable experiment.
source: George Santayana in The Life of Reason (1905), Vol. I, Reason in Common Sense.
sourceRaw: [[George Santayana]] in ''The Life of Reason'' (1905), Vol. I, ''Reason in Common Sense''.
author: George Santayana
textKo: 행복은 삶의 유일한 보증이다. 행복이 무너지는 곳에서 존재는 광적이고 한탄스러운 실험이 되어버린다.

text: The greatest happiness you can have is knowing that you do not necessarily require happiness.
source: William Saroyan, My Heart's in the Highlands (1939).
sourceRaw: [[William Saroyan]], ''My Heart's in the Highlands'' (1939).
author: William Saroyan
textKo: 네가 가질 수 있는 가장 큰 행복은, 너에게 반드시 행복이 필요한 것은 아님을 아는 것이다.

text: Let us meditate on the love of God, who being supremely happy Himself, communicateth perfect happiness to us. Supreme happiness doth not make God forget us; shall the miserable comforts of this life make us forget Him?
source: James Saurin reported in Josiah Hotchkiss Gilbert, Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895), p. 270.
sourceRaw: [[James Saurin]] reported in Josiah Hotchkiss Gilbert, ''Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers'' (1895), p. 270.
author: James Saurin
textKo: 자신은 지극히 행복하시면서도 우리에게 완전한 행복을 전하시는 신의 사랑을 묵상하자. 지극한 행복도 신께서 우리를 잊으시지 않게 하는데, 이 삶의 비참한 위로가 어떻게 우리로 하여금 그분을 잊게 할 수 있겠는가?

text: No man can live a happy life, or even a supportable life, without the study of wisdom.
source: Seneca the Younger, Moral Letters, R. Gummere, trans. (1917)
sourceRaw: [[Seneca the Younger]], ''Moral Letters'', R. Gummere, trans. (1917)
author: Seneca the Younger
textKo: 지혜를 공부하지 않고는 누구도 행복한 삶은커녕 견딜 만한 삶조차 살 수 없다.
