textKo: 평화의 조건은 정치 지도자들이 협상할지 모르나, 평화의 운명은 우리 각자에게 달려 있다.

text: Justice will win — because might does not make right, and the only path to lasting peace is when people know that their dignity will be respected and that their rights will be upheld.
source: Barack Obama, Remarks by President Obama to the People of Estonia i.e. students, young professionals, civil leaders, and the people of Estonia at the Nordea Concert Hall in Tallinn, Estonia on (3 September 2014)
sourceRaw: [[Barack Obama]], [http://www.whitehouse.gov/photos-and-video/video/2014/09/03/president-obama-addresses-people-estonia#transcript Remarks by President Obama to the People of Estonia i.e. students, young professionals, civil leaders, and the people of Estonia at the Nordea Concert Hall in Tallinn, Estonia] [http://www.whitehouse.gov/blog/2014/09/03/we-are-stronger-because-we-are-democracies-president-obama-addresses-people-estonia on (3 September 2014)]
author: Barack Obama
textKo: 정의는 승리할 것이다 — 힘이 옳음을 만들지 않기 때문이며, 지속적인 평화에 이르는 유일한 길은 사람들이 자기 존엄이 존중받고 자기 권리가 지켜진다는 것을 알 때이기 때문이다.

text: But he understood from hard-earned experience that true security comes through making peace with your neighbors.
source: Barack Obama, Remarks by President Obama at Memorial Service for Former Israeli President Shimon Peres on Mount Herzl in Jerusalem, Israel. (30 September 2016)
sourceRaw: [[Barack Obama]], [https://www.whitehouse.gov/the-press-office/2016/09/30/remarks-president-obama-memorial-service-former-israeli-president-shimon Remarks by President Obama at Memorial Service for Former Israeli President Shimon Peres on Mount Herzl in Jerusalem, Israel.] (30 September 2016)
author: Barack Obama
textKo: 그러나 그는 힘들게 얻은 경험에서, 진정한 안전은 이웃들과 평화를 맺는 데서 온다는 것을 이해했다.

text: Five enemies of peace inhabit with us — avarice, ambition, envy, anger, and pride; if these were to be banished, we should infallibly enjoy perpetual peace.
source: Petrarch, De vita solitaria (1346) as quoted in Wisdom for the Soul: Five Millennia of Prescriptions for Spiritual Healing‎ (2006) by Larry Chang, p. 144
sourceRaw: [[Petrarch]], ''De vita solitaria'' (1346) as quoted in ''Wisdom for the Soul: Five Millennia of Prescriptions for Spiritual Healing‎'' (2006) by Larry Chang, p. 144
author: Petrarch
textKo: 평화의 다섯 적이 우리와 함께 산다 — 탐욕·야망·시기·분노·교만. 이것들이 추방된다면 우리는 어김없이 영원한 평화를 누리게 될 것이다.

text: Allay the ferment prevailing in America by removing the obnoxious hostile cause—obnoxious and unserviceable—for their merit can only be in action. "Non dimicare et vincare."
source: William Pitt the Elder, speech (Jan. 20, 1775); referring to the American Colonies
sourceRaw: [[William Pitt the Elder]], speech (Jan. 20, 1775); referring to the American Colonies
author: William Pitt the Elder
textKo: 미국에 만연한 동요를 누그러뜨려라 — 그 미운, 적대적인 원인을 — 제거함으로써. '싸우지 않고 이기다.'

text: So long as [men] hold the tribal notion that the individual is sacrificial fodder for the collective, that some men have the right to rule others by force, and that some (any) alleged 'good' can justify It — there can be no peace ‘within’ a nation and no peace among nations.
source: Ayn Rand, Capitalism: The Unknown Ideal, “The Roots of War” chap., New York: NY, A Signal Book (1967) p. 42
sourceRaw: Ayn Rand, ''Capitalism: The Unknown Ideal'', “The Roots of War” chap., New York: NY, A Signal Book (1967) p. 42
author: Ayn Rand
textKo: 개인이 집단을 위한 희생 제물이라는 부족적 관념을, 어떤 사람들이 다른 이들을 무력으로 다스릴 권리가 있다는 관념을, 그리고 어떤 (어떤이든) 이른바 '선'이 그것을 정당화할 수 있다는 관념을 그들이 붙들고 있는 한 — 한 국가 '안'에도 평화는 없고, 국가들 사이에도 평화는 없다.

text: Peace is not the absence of conflict, but the ability to cope with conflict by peaceful means.
source: Ronald Reagan, "Address at Commencement Exercises at Eureka College in Illinois," May 9, 1982. Online by Gerhard Peters and John T. Woolley, The American Presidency Project.
sourceRaw: [[Ronald Reagan]], [http://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/ws/?pid=42501 "Address at Commencement Exercises at Eureka College in Illinois," May 9, 1982. Online by Gerhard Peters and John T. Woolley, The American Presidency Project.]
author: Ronald Reagan
textKo: 평화는 충돌의 부재가 아니라, 평화로운 수단으로 충돌에 대처하는 능력이다.

text: We wish peace, but we wish the peace of justice, the peace of righteousness. We wish it because we think it is right and not because we are afraid.
source: Theodore Roosevelt, Inaugural Address (6 September 1901)
sourceRaw: [[Theodore Roosevelt]], Inaugural Address (6 September 1901)
author: Theodore Roosevelt
textKo: 우리는 평화를 원한다. 그러나 우리는 정의의 평화, 의로움의 평화를 원한다. 우리가 그것을 원하는 것은 그것이 옳다고 생각하기 때문이지, 우리가 두려워서가 아니다.

text: America's own rightful place in the world depends in large part upon how fully these and similar rights have been carried into practice for all our citizens. For unless there is security here at home there cannot be lasting peace in the world.
source: Franklin D. Roosevelt, State of the Union Address — Second Bill of Rights (1944)
sourceRaw: [[Franklin D. Roosevelt]], State of the Union Address — Second Bill of Rights (1944)
author: Franklin D. Roosevelt
textKo: 세상에서 미국의 정당한 자리는, 이 권리들이 우리 모든 시민에게 얼마나 충실히 실천되었느냐에 크게 달려 있다. 이 땅에 안전이 없다면 세상에 지속적인 평화도 있을 수 없기 때문이다.

text: We can gain no lasting peace if we approach it with suspicion and mistrust or with fear. We can gain it only if we proceed with the understanding, the confidence, and the courage which flow from conviction.
source: Franklin D. Roosevelt, Fourth Inaugural Address (20 January 1945)
sourceRaw: [[Franklin D. Roosevelt]], [[s:Franklin Roosevelt's Fourth Inaugural Address|Fourth Inaugural Address (20 January 1945)]]
author: Franklin D. Roosevelt
textKo: 의심·불신·두려움으로 다가가서는 결코 지속적인 평화를 얻을 수 없다. 신념에서 흘러나오는 이해·자신감·용기로 나아갈 때에만 평화를 얻을 수 있다.

text: Peace is the music of every soul. Our glory lies in understanding, listening and honoring that music.
source: Amit Ray, Walking the Path of Compassion (2015)
sourceRaw: [[Amit Ray]], Walking the Path of Compassion (2015)
author: Amit Ray
textKo: 평화는 모든 영혼의 음악이다. 우리의 영광은 그 음악을 이해하고 듣고 존중하는 데 있다.

text: Sometimes there's truth in old cliches. There can be no real peace without justice. And without resistance there will be no justice.
source: Arundhati Roy, speech on Accepting the Sydney Peace Prize (7 November 2004) Sydney IMC article - Peace?... Full speech
sourceRaw: [[Arundhati Roy]], speech on Accepting the Sydney Peace Prize (7 November 2004) [http://sydney.indymedia.org/front.php3?article_id=48189&group=webcast Sydney IMC article] - [http://www.zmag.org/content/showarticle.cfm?SectionID=41&ItemID=6594 Peace?... Full speech]
author: Arundhati Roy
textKo: 때로 오래된 진부한 말에도 진실이 있다 — 정의 없이는 진정한 평화도 없다. 그리고 저항 없이는 정의도 없다.

text: peace is not lack of war, but a drive toward unity
source: Muriel Rukeyser The Life of Poetry (1949) p 210
sourceRaw: [[Muriel Rukeyser]] ''The Life of Poetry'' (1949) p 210
author: Muriel Rukeyser
textKo: 평화는 전쟁의 부재가 아니라, 통합을 향한 추진력이다.

text: You may assuredly find perfect peace, if you are resolved to do that which your Lord has plainly required,— and content that He should indeed require no more of you,— than to do justice, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with Him.
source: John Ruskin, as quoted in Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895), p. 446
sourceRaw: [[John Ruskin]], as quoted in ''Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers'' (1895), p. 446
author: John Ruskin
textKo: 네가 너의 주께서 분명히 요구하신 것을 행하기로 결심하고 — 그분이 정말 그 이상은 요구하지 않으심에 만족한다면 — 너는 분명 완전한 평화를 발견할 수 있다. 곧 정의를 행하고, 자비를 사랑하고, 너의 신과 함께 겸손히 걷는 것.

text: If peace cannot be maintained with honor, it is no longer peace.
source: Lord John Russell, speech at Greenoch (September 1853), as reported in Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations (1922), p. 588-91
sourceRaw: [[Lord John Russell]], speech at Greenoch (September 1853), as reported in ''Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations'' (1922), p. 588-91
author: Lord John Russell
textKo: 명예와 함께 유지될 수 없는 평화는 더 이상 평화가 아니다.

text: The process of peace and pacification is a work that requires long breath, like a marathon.
source: Catherine Samba-Panza, as quoted on GWToday, "Leader of the Central African Republic in Roundtable at GW" (2 March 2016)
sourceRaw: [[Catherine Samba-Panza]], as quoted on ''GWToday'', [https://gwtoday.gwu.edu/leader-central-african-republic-roundtable-gw "Leader of the Central African Republic in Roundtable at GW"] (2 March 2016)
author: Catherine Samba-Panza
textKo: 평화와 화평의 과정은 마라톤처럼 긴 호흡을 요하는 일이다.

text: "O mother, a strife like the black clouds' And a peace that cometh after.""Hush, child, for peace is the end of life,And the heart of a maiden finds peace as a wife,But the sky and the cliffs and the ocean are rife With the storm and thunder's laughter."
source: Frederick George Scott, "The Feud", st. 4, in Poems (London, 1936)
sourceRaw: [[Frederick George Scott]], "The Feud", st. 4, in ''Poems'' (London, 1936)
author: Frederick George Scott
textKo: '오 어머니, 검은 구름 같은 다툼과 그 뒤에 오는 평화여.' '쉿, 아이야, 평화는 삶의 끝이며, 처녀의 마음은 아내가 되어 평화를 찾는단다. 그러나 하늘과 절벽과 바다는 폭풍과 천둥의 웃음으로 가득하단다.'

text: Until he extends the circle of his compassion to all living things, man will not himself find peace.
source: Albert Schweitzer, Kulturphilosophie (1923)
sourceRaw: [[Albert Schweitzer]], ''Kulturphilosophie'' (1923)
author: Albert Schweitzer
textKo: 인간이 자신의 자비의 원을 모든 살아 있는 것에까지 넓히기 전에는, 인간 자신도 평화를 찾지 못할 것이다.

text: A peace is of the nature of a conquest;For then both parties nobly are subdued,And neither party loser.
source: William Shakespeare, Henry IV, Part II (c. 1597-99), Act IV, scene 2, line 89
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], [[Henry IV, Part 2|''Henry IV'', Part II]] (c. 1597-99), Act IV, scene 2, line 89
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 평화는 정복의 본성을 지녔다. 그때엔 양쪽 모두가 고귀하게 제압되며, 어느 쪽도 패자가 아니다.

text: In peace there's nothing so becomes a manAs modest stillness and humility.
source: William Shakespeare, Henry V (c. 1599), Act III, scene 1, line 3
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Henry V (play)|Henry V]]'' (c. 1599), Act III, scene 1, line 3
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 평화 시에 사람을 가장 사람답게 만드는 것은 겸손한 고요와 겸손이다.

text: * Peace,Dear nurse of arts, plenties and joyful births.
source: William Shakespeare, Henry V (c. 1599), Act V, scene 2, line 34
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Henry V (play)|Henry V]]'' (c. 1599), Act V, scene 2, line 34
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 평화여, 예술과 풍요와 기쁜 탄생의 사랑스러운 유모여.

text: Still in thy right hand carry gentle peace,To silence envious tongues.
source: William Shakespeare, Henry VIII (c. 1613), Act III, scene 2, line 445
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Henry VIII (play)|Henry VIII]]'' ([[w:Henry VIII (play)#Date|c. 1613]]), Act III, scene 2, line 445
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 여전히 너의 오른손에 부드러운 평화를 들고 다녀라 — 시기하는 혀들을 침묵시키기 위해.

text: I think people who work on translation projects think that they're somehow peace negotiators because the belief is that we'll never stop killing one another until we understand and see one another as human beings. I think that's true.
source: Naomi Shihab Nye Interview with Al Jadid (1996)
sourceRaw: [[Naomi Shihab Nye]] [https://www.aljadid.com/content/talking-poet-naomi-shihab-nye Interview] with Al Jadid (1996)
author: Naomi Shihab Nye
textKo: 번역 프로젝트에 종사하는 사람들은 자신이 어떤 의미에서 평화 협상가라 생각한다. 우리가 서로를 이해하고 인간으로 볼 때까지는 서로 죽이기를 멈추지 않을 것이라는 믿음 때문이다. 나는 그것이 사실이라 생각한다.

text: Truth is its [justice's] handmaid, freedom is its child, peace is its companion, safety walks in its steps, victory follows in its train; it is the brightest emanation from the Gospel; it is the attribute of God.
source: Sydney Smith, as quoted in Bartlett's Familiar Quotations, 10th ed. (1919),Volume I, p. 29
sourceRaw: [[Sydney Smith]], as quoted in ''Bartlett's Familiar Quotations'', 10th ed. (1919),Volume I, p. 29
author: Sydney Smith
textKo: 진리는 정의의 시녀이며, 자유는 정의의 자식이고, 평화는 정의의 동반자이며, 안전은 정의의 발자취를 따르고, 승리는 정의의 행렬을 뒤따른다. 정의는 복음에서 가장 밝게 발산되는 빛이며, 신의 속성이다.

text: History writes the word 'Reconciliation' over all her quarrels.
source: Jan Smuts to Alfred Milner (1905), as cited in Antony Lentin, 2010, Jan Smuts - Man of courage and vision
sourceRaw: [[Jan Smuts]] to [[w:Alfred Milner, 1st Viscount Milner|Alfred Milner]] (1905), as cited in Antony Lentin, 2010, Jan Smuts - Man of courage and vision {{ISBN|978-1-86842-390-3}}
author: Jan Smuts
textKo: 역사는 그 모든 다툼 위에 '화해'라는 단어를 적는다.

text: In this surrender—if such it may be called—the National Government does not even stoop to conquer. It simply lifts itself to the height of its original principle. The early efforts of its best negotiators, the patriotic trial of its soldiers … may at last prevail.
source: Charles Sumner, sustaining President Lincoln in the U.S. Senate, in the Trent Affair (7 January 1862)
sourceRaw: [[Charles Sumner]], sustaining President Lincoln in the U.S. Senate, in the Trent Affair (7 January 1862)
author: Charles Sumner
textKo: 이 굴복 — 만약 그렇게 부를 수 있다면 — 에서, 국가 정부는 정복을 위해 굽히지조차 않는다. 그저 자신의 본래 원칙의 높이로 자신을 들어 올릴 뿐이다.

text: Auferre, trucidare, rapere, falsis nominibus imperium, atque, ubi solitudinem faciunt, pacem appellant.
source: To rob, to ravage, to murder, in their imposing language, are the arts of civil policy. When they have made the world a solitude, they call it peace. — Tacitus, in Agricola, XXX, ascribing the speech to Galgacus, Britain's leader against the Romans, as reported in Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations (1922), p. 588-91
sourceRaw: To rob, to ravage, to murder, in their imposing language, are the arts of civil policy. When they have made the world a solitude, they call it peace. — [[Tacitus]], in ''Agricola'', XXX, ascribing the speech to Galgacus, Britain's leader against the Romans, as reported in ''Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations'' (1922), p. 588-91
author: To rob
textKo: 빼앗고, 살육하고, 약탈하기를, 그들은 거짓 이름으로 '제국'이라 부른다. 그리고 황무지를 만들고는 그것을 — 평화라 부른다. [원문 라틴어, 타키투스]

text: No more shall * * * PeacePipe on her pastoral hillock a languid note,And watch her harvest ripen.
source: Alfred Tennyson, Maud; A Monodrama (1855), Stanza 28
sourceRaw: [[Alfred Tennyson]], ''Maud; A Monodrama'' (1855), Stanza 28
author: Alfred Tennyson
textKo: 평화가 그 목가적 언덕 위에서 더 이상 나른한 가락을 불며 자기 추수가 익기를 지켜보지 않으리라.

text: Peace is the diploma you get in the cemetery.
source: Peter Tosh, as quoted in John Masouri (2013), Steppin' Razor: The Life of Peter Tosh, London: Omnibus Press.
sourceRaw: Peter Tosh, as quoted in John Masouri (2013), ''[https://books.google.com/books?id=vDn_AgAAQBAJ&pg=PT254 Steppin' Razor: The Life of Peter Tosh]'', London: Omnibus Press.
author: Peter Tosh
textKo: 평화는 묘지에서 받는 졸업장이다.

text: Peace will come wherever it is sincerely invited.
source: Alice Walker in Living by the Word : Selected Writings, 1973-1987 (1989), p. 192
sourceRaw: [[Alice Walker]] in ''Living by the Word : Selected Writings, 1973-1987'' (1989), p. 192<!-- Houghton Mifflin Harcourt -->
author: Alice Walker
textKo: 평화는 진심으로 초대되는 곳에는 어디든 올 것이다.

text: To be prepared for war is one of the most effectual means of preserving peace.
source: George Washington, First Annual Address, to both Houses of Congress (8 January 1790). — Compare: "Qui desiderat pacem præparet bellum" (translated: "Who would desire peace should be prepared for war"), Vegetius, Rei Militari 3, Prolog.; "In pace, ut sapiens, aptarit idonea bello" (translated: "In peace, as a wise man, he should make suitable preparation for war"), Horace, Book ii. satire ii.
sourceRaw: [[George Washington]], First Annual Address, to both Houses of Congress (8 January 1790). — Compare: "Qui desiderat pacem præparet bellum" (translated: "Who would desire peace should be prepared for war"), [[w:Publius Flavius Vegetius Renatus|Vegetius]], ''Rei Militari'' 3, Prolog.; "In pace, ut sapiens, aptarit idonea bello" (translated: "In peace, as a wise man, he should make suitable preparation for war"), [[Horace]], Book ii. satire ii.
author: George Washington
textKo: 전쟁을 대비하는 것은 평화를 보존하는 가장 효과적인 수단 중 하나다.

text: Observe good faith and justice towards all Nations; cultivate peace and harmony with all.
source: George Washington, in his Farewell Address (17 September 1796)
sourceRaw: [[George Washington]], in his Farewell Address (17 September 1796)
author: George Washington
textKo: 모든 나라에 대해 신의와 정의를 지켜라. 모든 이와 평화와 조화를 가꾸어라.

text: But dream not helm and harness The sign of valor true;Peace hath higher tests of manhood Than battle ever knew.
source: John Greenleaf Whittier, "The Hero", Stanza 19, in The Panorama and Other Poems (1856)
sourceRaw: [[John Greenleaf Whittier]], "The Hero", Stanza 19, in ''The Panorama and Other Poems'' (1856)
author: John Greenleaf Whittier
textKo: 투구와 갑옷이 참된 용기의 표지라고 꿈도 꾸지 마라. 평화에는 전쟁이 결코 알지 못한, 더 높은 사내다움의 시험이 있다.

text: As on the Sea of Galilee,The Christ is whispering "Peace."
source: John Greenleaf Whittier, in "Kallundborg Church", in Tent on the Beach (1867)
sourceRaw: [[John Greenleaf Whittier]], in "Kallundborg Church", in ''Tent on the Beach'' (1867)
author: John Greenleaf Whittier
textKo: 갈릴리 바다에서처럼, 그리스도가 속삭이신다 — '평화'.

text: The US will be a violent society until we decide to be nonviolent. Our task, if we do decide that, is to proactively and intentionally wage peace.
source: Marianne Williamson, Twitter (25 Oct 2019)
sourceRaw: [[Marianne Williamson]], [https://twitter.com/marwilliamson Twitter] (25 Oct 2019)
author: Marianne Williamson
textKo: 미국은 우리가 비폭력하기로 결정할 때까지는 폭력적인 사회로 남을 것이다. 그렇게 결정한다면, 우리의 과제는 능동적이고 의도적으로 평화를 일으키는 것이다.

text: There is a price which is too great to pay for peace, and that price can be put in one word. One cannot pay the price of self-respect.
source: Woodrow Wilson, Des Moines Iowa speech (1 February 1916), on "The Westerm Preparedness Tour"
sourceRaw: [[Woodrow Wilson]], [http://www.combat.ws/S3/BAKISSUE/CMBT01N2/SMOKE.HTM Des Moines Iowa speech (1 February 1916)], on [http://www.allthingswilliam.com/presidents/wilson.html "The Westerm Preparedness Tour"]
author: Woodrow Wilson
textKo: 평화를 위해 치를 수 없는 너무 큰 값이 하나 있으니, 그 값은 한 단어로 표현할 수 있다 — 자존심. 자존심의 값은 치를 수 없다.

text: It must be a peace without victory. . . . Only a peace between equals can last. Only a peace the very principle of which is equality and a common participation in a common benefit.
source: Woodrow Wilson, Speech to U.S. Senate on essential terms of peace in Europe (22 January 1917); in Albert Shaw, ed., The Messages and Papers of Woodrow Wilson (1924), vol. 1, p. 352
sourceRaw: [[Woodrow Wilson]], [http://www.allthingswilliam.com/presidents/wilson.html Speech to U.S. Senate on essential terms of peace in Europe] (22 January 1917); in Albert Shaw, ed., ''The Messages and Papers of Woodrow Wilson'' (1924), vol. 1, p. 352
author: Woodrow Wilson
textKo: 그것은 승리 없는 평화여야 한다… 오직 동등한 자들 사이의 평화만이 지속될 수 있다. 그 원칙 자체가 평등이며, 공동의 이익에 함께 참여하는 평화만이.

text: There must be, not a balance of power, but a community of power; not organized rivalries, but an organized common peace.
source: Woodrow Wilson, Address to the U.S. Senate (22 January 1917)
sourceRaw: [[Woodrow Wilson]], [http://www.allthingswilliam.com/presidents/wilson.html Address to the U.S. Senate (22 January 1917)]
author: Woodrow Wilson
textKo: 권력의 균형이 아니라, 권력의 공동체가 있어야 한다. 조직된 경쟁이 아니라, 조직된 공동의 평화가 있어야 한다.

text: What is at stake now is the peace of the world. What we are striving for is a new international order based upon broad and universal principles of right and justice, — no mere peace of shreds and patches.
source: Woodrow Wilson, "Address to Congress: Analyzing German and Austrian Peace Utterances", delivered to the U.S. Congress in Joint Session on (11 February 1918)
sourceRaw: [[Woodrow Wilson]], [http://www.gwpda.org/1918/wilpeace.html "Address to Congress: Analyzing German and Austrian Peace Utterances"], delivered to the U.S. Congress in Joint Session on (11 February 1918)
author: Woodrow Wilson
textKo: 지금 걸려 있는 것은 세계의 평화다. 우리가 추구하는 것은 옳음과 정의의 넓고 보편적인 원칙들에 기초한 새로운 국제 질서다 — 단순한 누더기 같은 평화가 아니다.

text: Ne'er to meet, or ne'er to part, is peace.
source: Edward Young, Night Thoughts (1742-1745), Night V, line 1,058
sourceRaw: [[Edward Young]], ''Night Thoughts'' (1742-1745), Night V, line 1,058
author: Edward Young
textKo: 결코 만나지 않거나 결코 헤어지지 않는 것이 평화다.

text: Even the best must ownPatience and resignation are the pillarsOf human peace on earth.
source: Edward Young, Night Thoughts (1742-1745), Night VIII, line 1,049
sourceRaw: [[Edward Young]], ''Night Thoughts'' (1742-1745), Night VIII, line 1,049
author: Edward Young
textKo: 가장 훌륭한 자조차도 인정해야 한다 — 인내와 체념이 이 땅에서 인간 평화의 기둥임을.

text: When we open up about our emotional challenges, admitting we are not perfect, we give others permission to share their struggles. Together we realize there is hope and we do not have to suffer alone.
source: Reyna I. Aburto, "Thru Cloud and Sunshine, Lord, Abide with Me!", Liahona (November 2019)
sourceRaw: [[Reyna I. Aburto]], [https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/liahona/2019/11/31aburto?lang=eng "Thru Cloud and Sunshine, Lord, Abide with Me!"], ''Liahona'' (November 2019)
author: Reyna I. Aburto
textKo: 우리가 자신의 정서적 어려움에 대해 마음을 열고 우리가 완벽하지 않음을 인정할 때, 우리는 다른 이들에게도 자기 분투를 나눌 수 있는 허락을 주는 것이다. 함께라면 우리는 희망이 있음을, 혼자 고통받을 필요가 없음을 깨닫는다.

text: When people talk of the Freedom of Writing, Speaking, or thinking, I cannot choose but laugh. No such thing ever existed. No such thing now exists; but I hope it will exist. But it must be hundreds of years after you and I shall write and speak no more.
source: John Adams Letter to Thomas Jefferson (15 July 1817)
sourceRaw: [[John Adams]] Letter to Thomas Jefferson (15 July 1817)
author: John Adams
textKo: 사람들이 글·말·생각의 자유를 말하면 나는 웃지 않을 수 없다. 그런 것은 결코 존재한 적 없고, 지금도 없다. 그러나 언젠가 존재하기를 바란다. 다만 그것은 너와 내가 더 이상 쓰지도 말하지도 못할 시점에서 수백 년 후의 일이리라.

text: If thy hope be any thing worth, it will purify thee from thy sins.
source: Joseph Alleine, The Solemn Warnings of the Dead: or, An Admonition to Unconverted Sinners (1804), Chapter 3, p. 44
sourceRaw: [[Joseph Alleine]], ''The Solemn Warnings of the Dead: or, An Admonition to Unconverted Sinners'' (1804), Chapter 3, p. 44
author: Joseph Alleine
textKo: 너의 희망이 무엇이든 가치 있는 것이라면, 그것은 너를 죄로부터 정화할 것이다.

text: For a moment hope, bright and cruel as a knife, presented itself to me. It took every ounce of strength I had to turn away.
source: C. L. Anderson, Bitter Angels (2009), Chapter 7
sourceRaw: [[Sarah Zettel|C. L. Anderson]], ''Bitter Angels'' (2009), Chapter 7
author: Sarah Zettel
textKo: 한순간 희망이 칼처럼 밝고 잔인하게 내 앞에 나타났다. 그것에서 등을 돌리는 데에 내 모든 힘이 필요했다.

text: This is what hope does to you when you’re not used to it. It is very like being drunk. You don’t realize how badly you’re impaired until you see the results of your spree.
source: C. L. Anderson, Bitter Angels (2009), Chapter 20
sourceRaw: [[Sarah Zettel|C. L. Anderson]], ''Bitter Angels'' (2009), Chapter 20
author: Sarah Zettel
textKo: 이것이 익숙하지 않을 때 희망이 너에게 미치는 효과다. 그것은 술에 취한 것과 매우 비슷하다. 그 광태의 결과를 보기 전까지는 자신이 얼마나 손상되었는지 깨닫지 못한다.

text: Know then, whatever cheerful and serene Supports the mind, supports the body too: Hence, the most vital movement mortals feel Is hope, the balm and lifeblood of the soul.
source: John Armstrong, Art of Preserving Health (1744), Book IV, line 310
sourceRaw: [[John Armstrong]], ''Art of Preserving Health'' (1744), Book IV, line 310
author: John Armstrong
textKo: 알라 — 마음을 지탱하는 명랑하고 평온한 것이라면 무엇이든 몸도 지탱한다. 그러므로 인간이 느끼는 가장 생명력 있는 움직임은 희망이다. 영혼의 향유이자 생혈인 희망이다.

text: Our greatest good, and what we least can spare, Is hope: the last of all our evils, fear.
source: John Armstrong, Art of Preserving Health (1744), Book IV, line 318
sourceRaw: [[John Armstrong]], ''Art of Preserving Health'' (1744), Book IV, line 318
author: John Armstrong
textKo: 우리의 가장 큰 선, 우리가 가장 적게 잃을 수 있는 것은 희망이다. 우리의 모든 악 중에서 마지막은 두려움이다.

text: Hope is a good breakfast, but it is a bad supper.
source: Francis Bacon, Apophthegms (1624), No. 36
sourceRaw: [[Francis Bacon]], ''Apophthegms'' (1624), No. 36
author: Francis Bacon
textKo: 희망은 좋은 아침식사지만, 나쁜 저녁식사다.

text: HOPE, n. Desire and expectation rolled into one.
source: Ambrose Bierce, The Cynic's Dictionary (1906); republished as The Devil's Dictionary (1911).
sourceRaw: [[Ambrose Bierce]], ''The Cynic's Dictionary'' (1906); republished as ''The Devil's Dictionary'' (1911).
author: Ambrose Bierce
textKo: 희망, 명사. 욕망과 기대가 하나로 뭉친 것.

text: Nature has fixed no limits on our hopes.
source: Björk, "Hope" on Volta (2007)
sourceRaw: [[Björk]], "Hope" on ''[[w:Volta (album)|Volta]]'' (2007)
author: Björk
textKo: 자연은 우리의 희망에 어떤 한계도 두지 않았다.

text: I live in hope and that I think do all Who come into this world.
source: Robert Bridges, The Growth of Love (1898), Sonnet 63
sourceRaw: [[Robert Bridges]], ''The Growth of Love'' (1898), Sonnet 63
author: Robert Bridges
textKo: 나는 희망 속에 산다. 그리고 이 세상에 오는 모든 이도 그렇다고 나는 생각한다.

text: The heart bowed down by weight of woe To weakest hope will cling.
source: Alfred Bunn, Bohemian Girl as reported in Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations (1922), p. 375-78
sourceRaw: [[Alfred Bunn]], ''Bohemian Girl'' as reported in ''Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations'' (1922), p. 375-78
author: Alfred Bunn
textKo: 슬픔의 무게에 짓눌린 마음은, 가장 희미한 희망에도 매달린다.

text: Hope springs exulting on triumphant wing.
source: Robert Burns, The Cotter's Saturday Night (1786), Stanza 16
sourceRaw: [[Robert Burns]], ''The Cotter's Saturday Night'' (1786), Stanza 16
author: Robert Burns
textKo: 희망은 승리의 날개를 펴며 환희에 차 솟아오른다.

text: But what is Hope? Nothing but the paint on the face of Existence. The least touch of truth rubs it off, and then we see what a hollow-cheeked harlot we have got hold of.
source: Lord Byron, letter to Thomas Moore, 28 October 1815, in Byrons Letters and Journals (1975), Vol 4, ed. Leslie Marchand
sourceRaw: [[Lord Byron]], letter to [[Thomas Moore]], 28 October 1815, in ''Byrons Letters and Journals'' (1975), Vol 4, ed. Leslie Marchand
author: Lord Byron
textKo: 그러나 희망이란 무엇인가? 다만 존재의 얼굴에 칠해진 분장일 뿐. 진실의 가벼운 손길에도 지워지고, 그러면 우리가 어떤 텅 빈 뺨의 매춘부를 붙들고 있었는지를 보게 된다.

text: Daughter of Faith, awake, arise, illume The dread unknown, the chaos of the tomb.
source: Thomas Campbell, "Pleasures of Hope", Part 2, St. 23; The Pleasures of Hope; With Other Poems (7th ed. 1803), p. 67
sourceRaw: [[Thomas Campbell]], "Pleasures of Hope", Part 2, St. 23; ''The Pleasures of Hope; With Other Poems'' (7th ed. 1803), [http://books.google.com/books?id=9vqTmFv8eCoC&pg=PA67 p. 67]
author: Thomas Campbell
textKo: 믿음의 딸이여, 깨어나 일어나라. 두려운 미지의 것을, 무덤의 혼돈을 비추라.

text: There's a hope that's waiting for you, in the dark.
source: Alessia Cara, "Scars to your Beautiful" (2015), Know-It-All
sourceRaw: Alessia Cara, "Scars to your Beautiful" (2015), ''Know-It-All''
author: Alessia Cara
textKo: 어둠 속에서 너를 기다리고 있는 희망이 있다.

text: Hope knows no fear. Hope dares to blossom even inside the abysmal abyss. Hope secretly feeds and strengthens promise.
source: Sri Chinmoy, My Christmas-New Year-Vacation-Aspiration-Prayers Part 26 (2003)
sourceRaw: [[Sri Chinmoy]], ''My Christmas-New Year-Vacation-Aspiration-Prayers Part 26 (2003)''
author: Sri Chinmoy
textKo: 희망은 두려움을 모른다. 희망은 심연의 바닥에서도 감히 꽃 핀다. 희망은 약속을 은밀히 먹이고 강하게 한다.

text: Work without hope draws nectar in a sieve, And hope without an object cannot live.
source: Samuel Taylor Coleridge, "Work Without Hope" (1825), Stanza 2
sourceRaw: [[Samuel Taylor Coleridge]], [http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/stc/Coleridge/poems/Work_without_Hope.html "Work Without Hope"] (1825), Stanza 2
author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
textKo: 희망 없는 노동은 체로 꿀을 뜨는 일이며, 대상 없는 희망은 살 수 없다.

text: And Hope enchanted smiled, and waved her golden hair.
source: William Collins, The Passions, an Ode for Music (1747), line 3
sourceRaw: [[William Collins]], ''The Passions, an Ode for Music'' (1747), line 3
author: William Collins
textKo: 그리고 희망이 황홀히 미소 지으며, 자기 황금 머리카락을 흔들었다.

text: But thou, O Hope, with eyes so fair, What was thy delighted measure? Still it whisper'd promised pleasure, And bade the lovely scenes at distance hail!
source: William Collins, The Passions, an Ode for Music (1747), line 29
sourceRaw: [[William Collins]], ''The Passions, an Ode for Music'' (1747), line 29
author: William Collins
textKo: 그러나 너, 오 희망이여, 그토록 아름다운 눈으로 — 너의 즐거운 가락은 무엇이었나? 여전히 약속된 즐거움을 속삭이며, 멀리 사랑스러운 장면들을 환영하게 했지!

text: When faith and hope fail, as they do sometimes, we must try charity, which is love in action. We must speculate no more on our duty, but simply do it. When we have done it, however blindly, perhaps Heaven will show us why.
source: Dinah Craik, Christian's Mistake (1865). p. 64
sourceRaw: [[Dinah Craik]], ''Christian's Mistake'' (1865). p. 64
author: Dinah Craik
textKo: 믿음과 희망이 — 가끔 그렇듯 — 실패할 때, 우리는 사랑 — 곧 행동하는 사랑 — 인 자비를 시도해야 한다. 의무에 대해 더 이상 사색하지 말고, 그저 행하라. 비록 맹목적으로라도 행하고 나면, 어쩌면 천국이 그 이유를 보여줄 것이다.

text: “As time progresses,” Lump stated, “people learn. That’s the only hope.”
source: Samuel R. Delany, Empire Star (1966), reprinted in David G. Hartwell (ed.), The Space Opera Renaissance, , p. 197
sourceRaw: [[Samuel R. Delany]], ''Empire Star'' (1966), reprinted in [[w:David G. Hartwell|David G. Hartwell]] (ed.), ''[[w:The Space Opera Renaissance|The Space Opera Renaissance]],'' {{ISBN|0-765-30618-2}}, p. 197
author: Samuel R. Delany
textKo: '시간이 지나면', 럼프는 말했다, '사람들은 배운다. 그것이 유일한 희망이다.'

text: "Hope" is the thing with feathers — That perches in the soul — And sings the tune without the words — And never stops — at all — And sweetest — in the Gale — is heard — And sore must be the storm — That could abash the little BirdThat kept so many warm —
source: Emily Dickinson, Poem 254 in The Complete Poems of Emily Dickinson (1960), edited by Thomas H. Johnson
sourceRaw: [[Emily Dickinson]], Poem 254 in ''The Complete Poems of Emily Dickinson'' (1960), edited by Thomas H. Johnson
author: Emily Dickinson
textKo: '희망'은 깃털 달린 것 — 영혼에 깃들고 — 가사 없는 가락을 부르며 — 결코 — 그치지 않는 것. 가장 달콤하게 — 폭풍 속에 — 들리니, 그토록 많은 이를 따뜻하게 했던 그 작은 새를 잠재울 폭풍은 — 참혹해야만 하리라.

text: Until the day when God will deign to reveal the future to man, all human wisdom is contained in these two words, Wait and hope.
source: Alexandre Dumas, The Count of Monte Cristo (1845), Chapter 117
sourceRaw: [[Alexandre Dumas]], ''The Count of Monte Cristo'' (1845), Chapter 117
author: Alexandre Dumas
textKo: 신께서 미래를 인간에게 드러내실 그날까지, 인간의 모든 지혜는 이 두 단어 안에 담겨 있다 — 기다리고, 희망하라.

text: Hope is many things, but it throws itself against fact and shatters.
source: Pete Dunne, The Feather Quest (1992), , p. 304
sourceRaw: [[Pete Dunne]], ''[[w:Pete Dunne (author)|The Feather Quest]]'' (1992), <small> {{ISBN|0-395-92790-0}}, </small> p. 304
author: Pete Dunne
textKo: 희망은 많은 것이지만, 그것은 사실에 부딪쳐 산산조각 난다.

text: Hopes have precarious life. They are oft blighted, withered, snapped sheer off In vigorous growth and turned to rottenness.
source: George Eliot, The Spanish Gypsy (1868), Book III
sourceRaw: [[George Eliot]], ''The Spanish Gypsy'' (1868), Book III
author: George Eliot
textKo: 희망은 위태로운 생명을 지녔다. 활발히 자라는 중에 흔히 시들고 말라 꺾이고, 부패로 변한다.

text: The only hope, or else despair Lies in the choice of pyre or pyre — To be redeemed from fire by fire.
source: T. S. Eliot, Four Quartets, Little Gidding (1942), (IV)
sourceRaw: [[T. S. Eliot]], [[Four Quartets]], ''Little Gidding (1942)'', (IV)
author: T. S. Eliot
textKo: 유일한 희망 — 혹은 절망 — 은 어떤 장작더미를 택하느냐에 있다. 불에서 불로 구원받는 것.

text: He that lives upon Hope will die fasting.
source: Benjamin Franklin, Poor Richard's Almanack (1758)
sourceRaw: [[Benjamin Franklin]], ''[[Poor Richard's Almanack]]'' (1758)
author: Benjamin Franklin
textKo: 희망에 기대어 사는 자는 굶어 죽으리라.

text: People cannot live without hope; this is one of the statements I can defend without any reservations.
source: Hans-Georg Gadamer in one of his last interviews, "Die Menschen können nicht ohne Hoffnung leben", Rhein-Neckar-Zeitung (February 11, 2002)
sourceRaw: [[Hans-Georg Gadamer]] in one of his last interviews, "Die Menschen können nicht ohne Hoffnung leben", ''Rhein-Neckar-Zeitung'' (February 11, 2002)
author: Hans-Georg Gadamer
textKo: 사람은 희망 없이는 살 수 없다 — 이것이 내가 한 치의 유보 없이 옹호할 수 있는 명제 중 하나다.

text: While there is life there's hope (he cried,) Then why such haste?—so groan'd and died.
source: John Gay, The Sick Man and The Angel, as reported in Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations (1922), p. 375-78
sourceRaw: [[John Gay]], ''The Sick Man and The Angel'', as reported in ''Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations'' (1922), p. 375-78
author: John Gay
textKo: '생명이 있는 동안엔 희망이 있다' — 그는 외쳤다 — '그렇다면 왜 그리 서두르는가?' 그렇게 신음하며 죽었다.

text: Wir hoffen immer, und in allen Dingen Ist besser hoffen als verzweifeln.
source: We always hope, and in all things it is better to hope than to despair. — Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, Torquato Tasso, III. 4. 197, as reported in Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations (1922), p. 375-78
sourceRaw: We always hope, and in all things it is better to hope than to despair. — [[Johann Wolfgang von Goethe]], ''Torquato Tasso'', III. 4. 197, as reported in ''Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations'' (1922), p. 375-78
author: We always hope
textKo: 우리는 늘 희망한다. 그리고 모든 일에서, 절망하기보다는 희망하는 편이 낫다. [원문 독일어, 괴테]

text: Hope keeps you focused on the future, and this continued focus perpetuates your denial of the Now and therefore your unhappiness.
source: Eckhart Tolle, The Power of Now
sourceRaw: [[Eckhart Tolle]], ''The Power of Now''
author: Eckhart Tolle
textKo: 희망은 너의 초점을 미래에 묶어둔다. 그리고 그 지속되는 초점이야말로 '지금'에 대한 너의 부정을, 그러므로 너의 불행을 영속시킨다.

text: He that lives in hope danceth without music.
source: English proverb, reported in George Herbert, Jacula Prudentum (1640), No. 1006
sourceRaw: English proverb, reported in [[George Herbert]], ''Jacula Prudentum'' (1640), No. 1006
workTitle: Anonymous
author: English proverb
textKo: 희망 속에 사는 자는 음악 없이도 춤춘다.

text: Hope for the best and prepare for the worst.
source: Traditional proverb, reported in Roger L'Estrange, Seneca's Morals (1702)
sourceRaw: Traditional proverb, reported in [[w:Roger L'Estrange|Roger L'Estrange]], ''Seneca's Morals'' (1702)
workTitle: Anonymous
author: Traditional proverb
textKo: 최선을 바라되 최악을 대비하라.

text: Wisdom is purified by morality, and morality is purified by wisdom: where one is, the other is, the moral man has wisdom and the wise man has morality, and the combination of morality and wisdom is called the highest thing in the world.
source: Gautama Buddha, Digha Nikaya, M. Walshe, trans. (1987), Sutta 4 (Sonadanda Sutta), verse 22, p. 131
sourceRaw: [[Gautama Buddha]], ''[[w:Digha Nikaya|Digha Nikaya]]'', M. Walshe, trans. (1987), Sutta 4 (Sonadanda Sutta), verse 22, p. 131
author: Gautama Buddha
textKo: 지혜는 도덕에 의해 정화되고, 도덕은 지혜에 의해 정화된다. 하나가 있으면 다른 하나도 있다. 도덕적인 사람에게 지혜가 있고, 지혜로운 사람에게 도덕이 있으니, 도덕과 지혜의 결합이야말로 세상에서 가장 높은 것이라 한다.

text: To finish the moment, to find the journey's end in every step of the road, to live the greatest number of good hours, is wisdom.
source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Essays: Second Series (1844), Experience
sourceRaw: [[Ralph Waldo Emerson]], ''[[wikisource:Essays: Second Series|Essays: Second Series]]'' (1844), ''Experience''
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
textKo: 순간을 완성하고, 길의 모든 걸음마다 여정의 끝을 발견하며, 가능한 한 많은 좋은 시간을 사는 것 — 그것이 지혜다.

text: Some are weather-wise, some are otherwise.
source: Benjamin Franklin, Poor Richard (1735)
sourceRaw: [[Benjamin Franklin]], ''Poor Richard'' (1735)

author: Benjamin Franklin

textKo: 어떤 이는 날씨를 잘 알고, 어떤 이는 그렇지 못하다.

text: Away, thou strange justifier of thyself, to be wiser than thou wert, by the event.
source: Ben Jonson, Silent Woman, Act II, scene 2. "Wise after the event." text: A little too wise they say do ne'er live long.
source: Thomas Middleton, The Phœnix (1603-04), Act I, scene 1
sourceRaw: [[Thomas Middleton]], ''The Phœnix'' (1603-04), Act I, scene 1

textKo: 지나치게 지혜로운 자는 결코 오래 살지 못한다고들 한다.

text: Wisdom does not show itself so much in precept as in life—in a firmness of mind and mastery of appetite. It teaches us to do, as well as to talk; and to make our actions and words all of a color.
source: Seneca the Younger, Epistles, XX
sourceRaw: [[Seneca the Younger]], ''Epistles'', XX
workTitle: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
author: Seneca the Younger
sectionPath: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
textKo: 지혜는 가르침보다 삶에서 — 마음의 굳건함과 욕망에 대한 절제에서 드러난다. 그것은 우리에게 말뿐 아니라 행동도 가르치며, 우리의 말과 행동을 같은 빛깔로 만들도록 가르친다.

text: The wise man is but a clever infant, spelling letters from a hieroglyphical prophetic book, the lexicon of which lies in eternity.
source: Thomas Carlyle, p. 617
sourceRaw: [[Thomas Carlyle]], p. 617
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Thomas Carlyle
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 지혜로운 자란, 영원에 사전이 있는 상형문자 예언서에서 글자를 더듬어 읽는 영리한 아이일 뿐이다.

text: What in me is dark, Illumine, what is low, raise and support.
source: John Milton, p. 617
sourceRaw: [[John Milton]], p. 617
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: John Milton
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 내 안의 어두운 것을 비추시고, 낮은 것을 일으켜 떠받쳐 주소서.

text: For knowledge to become wisdom, and for the soul to grow, the soul must be rooted in God: and it is through prayer that there comes to us that which is the strength of our strength, and the virtue of our virtue, the Holy Spirit.
source: William Mountford, p. 616
sourceRaw: [[William Mountford]], p. 616
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: William Mountford
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 지식이 지혜가 되고 영혼이 자라기 위해서는 영혼이 신께 뿌리내려야 한다. 그리고 우리에게 우리 힘의 힘이며 우리 덕의 덕인 것 — 곧 성령 — 이 임하는 것은 기도를 통해서다.

text: Drop, drop—in our sleep, upon the heartsorrow falls, memory's pain,and to us, though against our very will,even in our own despite,comes wisdomby the awful grace of God.
source: Aeschylus, Agamemnon. The above lines are from Edith Hamilton, trans., Three Greek Plays, p. 170 (1937). Other translations of this passage from Aeschylus vary. Robert F. Kennedy, delivering an extemporaneous eulogy to Martin Luther King, Jr., the evening of April 4, 1968, in Indianapolis, Indiana, said, "Aeschylus wrote: 'In our sleep, pain that cannot forget falls drop by drop upon the heart and in our own despair, against our will, comes wisdom through the awful grace of God.'" These words, lacking "own", have been used as one of the inscriptions at the Robert F. Kennedy gravesite in Arlington National Cemetery.

text: Ask counsel of both times—of the ancient time what is best, and of the latter time what is fittest.
source: Francis Bacon, "Of Great Place", The Essays, or Counsels Civil & Moral of Francis Bacon, p. 48 (1905). Based on the 1625 edition but with modernized spelling.
sourceRaw: [[Francis Bacon]], "Of Great Place", The Essays, or Counsels Civil & Moral of Francis Bacon, p. 48 (1905). Based on the 1625 edition but with modernized spelling.

text: Wisdom too often never comes, and so one ought not to reject it merely because it comes late.
source: Felix Frankfurter, Henslee v. Union Planters Bank, 335 U.S. 600 (1948) (dissenting)
sourceRaw: [[Felix Frankfurter]], ''Henslee v. Union Planters Bank'', 335 U.S. 600 (1948) (dissenting)

textKo: 지혜는 너무도 자주 결코 오지 않는다. 그러니 늦게 왔다는 이유만으로 그것을 거부해서는 안 된다.

text: Standing in this presence, mindful of the solemnity of this occasion, feeling the emotions which no one may know until he senses the great weight of responsibility for himself, I must utter my belief in the divine inspiration of the founding fathers.
source: Warren G. Harding, inaugural address, March 4, 1921. Inaugural Addresses of the Presidents of the United States from George Washington, 1789, to Richard Milhous Nixon, 1969, p. 207 (1969). House Doc. 91–142. Harding is credited with originating the phrase founding fathers. Senator Harding's remarks before the Sons and Daughters of the Revolution, Washington, D.C., February 22, 1918, included this sentence: "It is good to meet and drink at the fountains of wisdom inherited from the founding fathers of the Republic". Address on Washington's Birthday, p. 3 (1918). Senate Doc. 65–180. He also used the phrase in his speech on being officially notified of his nomination for the presidency, Marion, Ohio, July 22, 1920. According to "Of Deathless Remarks…", American Heritage, June 1970, p. 57, his 1918 remarks were "the first use of the phrase that the combined efforts of the experts at the Library of Congress have been able to find".

text: Pain makes man think. Thought makes man wise. Wisdom makes life endurable.
source: John Patrick, The Teahouse of the August Moon, act I, scene i, p. 6 (1957). These words are spoken by Sakini, an Okinawan, to the audience. They are repeated in act III, scene iii, and at the conclusion of the play.

textKo: 고통은 사람을 생각하게 하고, 생각은 사람을 지혜롭게 하며, 지혜는 삶을 견딜 만한 것으로 만든다.

text: Let gratitude be the pillow upon which you kneel to say your nightly prayer. And let faith be the bridge you build to overcome evil and welcome good.
source: Maya Angelou, Celebrations: Rituals of Peace and Prayer (2006)
sourceRaw: [[Maya Angelou]], ''Celebrations: Rituals of Peace and Prayer'' (2006)

author: Maya Angelou
textKo: 감사를 베개 삼아 무릎 꿇고 밤마다 기도하라. 그리고 믿음을 다리 삼아 악을 이기고 선을 맞이하라.

text: When prosperous the fool trembles for the evil that is to come; in adversity the philosopher smiles for the good that he has had.
source: Ambrose Bierce, Epigrams, The Collected Works of Ambrose Bierce (1911), Volume 8, p. 371.
sourceRaw: [[Ambrose Bierce]], ''Epigrams'', ''The Collected Works of Ambrose Bierce'' (1911), Volume 8, p. 371.

author: Ambrose Bierce
textKo: 번영할 때 어리석은 자는 다가올 악을 두려워하나, 역경 속에서 철학자는 자신이 누렸던 선에 미소 짓는다.

text: Nine-tenths of wisdom is appreciation. Go find somebody's hand and squeeze it, while there's time.
source: Dale Dauten, Cited in: Colleen Zuck etal. (2002) Daily Word for Families, p. 167.
sourceRaw: Dale Dauten, Cited in: Colleen Zuck etal. (2002) ''Daily Word for Families,'' p. 167.

text: When I'm not thank'd at all, I'm thank'd enough,I've done my duty, and I've done no more.
source: Henry Fielding, The Life and Death of Tom Thumb the Great (1730), Act I, scene 3.
sourceRaw: [[Henry Fielding]], ''The Life and Death of Tom Thumb the Great'' (1730), Act I, scene 3.
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude

textKo: 전혀 감사받지 못해도 나는 충분히 감사받았다. 나는 내 의무를 다했고, 그 이상은 하지 않았으니.

text: Gratitude and love. He wasn’t the only one who lived with the pretty lie that one must necessarily lead to the other.
source: Esther Friesner, Sphynxes Wild (1989), , p. 78
sourceRaw: [[Esther Friesner]], ''Sphynxes Wild'' (1989), <small> {{ISBN|0-451-15974-8}}, </small> p. 78

textKo: 감사와 사랑. 하나가 반드시 다른 하나로 이어진다는 그 예쁜 거짓말과 함께 살아간 사람은 그뿐이 아니었다.

text: Gratitude is a fruit of great cultivation; you do not find it among gross people.
source: Samuel Johnson, Tour to the Hebrides (Sept. 20, 1773).
sourceRaw: [[Samuel Johnson]], ''Tour to the Hebrides'' (Sept. 20, 1773).
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude
author: Samuel Johnson
textKo: 감사는 잘 가꾸어진 자만이 거두는 열매다. 거친 사람들에게서는 찾아볼 수 없다.

text: I am glad that he thanks God for anything.
source: Samuel Johnson, reported in James Boswell, Life of Samuel Johnson (1775).
sourceRaw: [[Samuel Johnson]], reported in [[James Boswell]], ''Life of Samuel Johnson'' (1775).
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude
author: Samuel Johnson
textKo: 무엇이든 그가 신께 감사한다는 것이 기쁘다.

text: Do not let the empty cup be your first teacher of the blessings you had when it was full. Do not let a hard place here and there in the bed destroy your rest. Seek, as a plain duty, to cultivate a buoyant, joyous sense of the crowded kindnesses of God in your daily life.
source: Alexander Maclaren, reported in Josiah Hotchkiss Gilbert, Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895), p. 290.
sourceRaw: [[Alexander Maclaren]], reported in Josiah Hotchkiss Gilbert, ''Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers'' (1895), p. 290.
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude
author: Alexander Maclaren
textKo: 빈 잔이 처음으로 그 잔이 가득했을 때 누렸던 축복을 가르치는 스승이 되게 하지 마라. 잠자리 여기저기의 단단한 자리가 너의 안식을 망치게 하지 마라. 분명한 의무로서, 매일의 삶 속에 넘쳐나는 신의 친절을 향한 활기차고 기쁜 자각을 가꾸기를 힘쓰라.

text: A grateful mindBy owing owes not, but still pays, at onceIndebted and discharg'd.
source: John Milton, Paradise Lost (1667; 1674), Book IV, line 55.
sourceRaw: [[John Milton]], ''[[Paradise Lost]]'' (1667; 1674), Book IV, line 55.
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude
author: John Milton
textKo: 감사하는 마음은 빚지면서도 빚지지 않으니, 늘 갚으면서도 빚지고 또 청산한다.

text: The gratitude of most men is but a secret desire of receiving greater benefits.
source: François de La Rochefoucauld, Reflections; or Sentences and Moral Maxims, Maxim 298 (1665–1678).
sourceRaw: [[François de La Rochefoucauld]], ''Reflections; or Sentences and Moral Maxims'', Maxim 298 (1665–1678).
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
textKo: 대부분 사람의 감사는 더 큰 은혜를 받고자 하는 은밀한 욕망일 뿐이다.

text: Your bounty is beyond my speaking;But though my mouth be dumb, my heart shall thank you.
source: Nicholas Rowe, Jane Shore (1714), Act II, scene 1.
sourceRaw: [[Nicholas Rowe]], ''Jane Shore'' (1714), Act II, scene 1.
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude
author: Nicholas Rowe
textKo: 당신의 은혜는 내가 말할 수 없을 만큼 크다. 비록 입은 벙어리일지라도, 내 마음은 당신께 감사하리라.

text: Now the good gods forbidThat our renowned Rome, whose gratitudeTowards her deserved children is enroll'dIn Jove's own book, like an unnatural damShould now eat up her own!
source: William Shakespeare, Coriolanus (c. 1607-08), Act III, scene 1, line 290.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Coriolanus]]'' (c. 1607-08), Act III, scene 1, line 290.
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 선한 신들이여 막아주소서. 받은 자녀들에 대한 감사가 유피테르의 책에 기록된 우리의 영광된 로마가, 마치 부자연스러운 어미처럼 자기 자식을 삼키는 일이 없게 하소서!

text: O Lord, that lends me life, Lend me a heart replete with thankfulness!
source: William Shakespeare, Henry VI, Part II (c. 1590-91), Act I, scene 1.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], [[Henry VI, Part 2|''Henry VI'', Part II]] (c. 1590-91), Act I, scene 1.
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 오 주여, 제게 생명을 빌려주신 분이여, 감사로 가득한 마음을 빌려주소서!

text: Let never day nor night unhallow'd pass,But still remember what the Lord hath done.
source: William Shakespeare, Henry VI, Part II (c. 1590-91), Act II, scene 1, line 85.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], [[Henry VI, Part 2|''Henry VI'', Part II]] (c. 1590-91), Act II, scene 1, line 85.
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 낮과 밤이 거룩하지 않게 지나가게 하지 마라. 주께서 행하신 일을 늘 기억하라.

text: How sharper than a serpent's tooth it isTo have a thankless child.
source: William Shakespeare, King Lear (1608), Act I, scene 4, line 310.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[King Lear|King Lear]]'' (1608), Act I, scene 4, line 310.
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude
author: William Shakespeare
textKo: 감사할 줄 모르는 자식을 두는 것은 뱀의 이빨보다 더 날카롭게 찌른다!

text: To receive honestly is the best thanks for a good thing.
source: George MacDonald, Mary Marston (1881), Chapter V.
sourceRaw: [[George MacDonald]], ''Mary Marston'' (1881), Chapter V.
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude
author: George MacDonald
textKo: 좋은 것에 대한 가장 진실한 감사는, 정직하게 받는 것이다.

text: The best way to be thankful is to use the goods the gods provide you.
source: Anthony Trollope, (1867), Vol. I, ch. 32.
sourceRaw: [[Anthony Trollope]], ''{{w|The Last Chronicle of Barset}}'' (1867), Vol. I, ch. 32.
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude
author: Anthony Trollope
textKo: 감사하는 가장 좋은 방법은 신들이 너에게 준 좋은 것을 사용하는 것이다.

text: If hush'd the loud whirlwind that ruffled the deep, The sky if no longer dark tempests deform;When our perils are past shall our gratitude sleep? No! Here's to the pilot that weather'd the storm!
source: George Canning, Song (on "Billy Pitt"); sung at a public dinner (May 28, 1802).
sourceRaw: [[George Canning]], ''Song'' (on "Billy Pitt"); sung at a public dinner (May 28, 1802).
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude
author: George Canning
sectionPath: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
textKo: 바다를 뒤흔들던 큰 폭풍이 잠잠해지고, 어두운 폭풍이 더 이상 하늘을 일그러뜨리지 않을 때 — 위험이 지나갔다고 우리의 감사가 잠들겠는가? 아니다! 폭풍을 헤쳐온 그 키잡이에게 건배를!

text: As we give thanks for the Earth, will we live in such a way that the Earth can be grateful for us?
source: Robin Wall Kimmerer Interview (2015)
sourceRaw: [[Robin Wall Kimmerer]] [https://www.potawatomi.org/blog/2015/11/03/q-a-with-robin-wall-kimmerer-ph-d/ Interview] (2015)
workTitle: Quotes Gratitude
author: Robin Wall Kimmerer
sectionPath: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
textKo: 우리가 대지에 감사를 드리는 동안, 우리는 과연 대지가 우리에게 감사할 만한 방식으로 살아갈 것인가?

text: When death, the great Reconciler, has come, it is never our tenderness that we repent of, but our severity.
source: George Eliot, p. 578.
sourceRaw: [[George Eliot]], p. 578.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: George Eliot
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 위대한 화해자인 죽음이 왔을 때, 우리가 후회하는 것은 결코 우리의 다정함이 아니라 우리의 가혹함이다.

text: I was never fit to say a word to a sinner, except when I had a broken heart myself.
source: Edward Payson, p. 579.
sourceRaw: [[Edward Payson]], p. 579.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Edward Payson
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 내가 스스로 상한 마음을 가져본 적 있을 때 외에는, 죄인에게 단 한 마디 건넬 자격조차 없었다.

text: Put from you the belief that "I have been wronged", and with it will go the feeling. Reject your sense of injury, and the injury itself disappears.
source: Marcus Aurelius, in Meditations, as cited to a 1995 translation, p. 19, in The Future of Counselling and Psychotherapy (1997) by Stephen Palmer and Ved P. Varma, Ch. 6, p. 84 — Variant translations: — Let opinion be taken away, and no man will think himself wronged. If no man shall think himself wronged, then is there no more any such thing as wrong. That which makes not man himself the worse, cannot make his life the worse, neither can it hurt him either inwardly or outwardly. It was expedient in nature that it should be so, and therefore necessary. — Book IV, § 7, as translated by Meric Causubon (1906)
sourceRaw: [[Marcus Aurelius]], in ''Meditations'', as cited to a 1995 translation, p. 19, in ''The Future of Counselling and Psychotherapy'' (1997) by Stephen Palmer and Ved P. Varma, Ch. 6, p. 84<!-- also in ''Creating a Balance: Managing Stress''(2005), by Stephen Palmer, Cary L. Cooper, and Kate Thomas, p. 3 -->  — Variant translations: — Let opinion be taken away, and no man will think himself wronged. If no man shall think himself wronged, then is there no more any such thing as wrong. That which makes not man himself the worse, cannot make his life the worse, neither can it hurt him either inwardly or outwardly. It was expedient in nature that it should be so, and therefore necessary. — Book IV, § 7, as translated by Meric Causubon (1906)
author: Marcus Aurelius
textKo: '나는 부당한 일을 당했다'는 믿음을 버려라. 그러면 그 감정도 함께 사라진다. 상처받았다는 느낌을 거부하라. 그러면 상처 자체가 사라진다.

text: His heart was as great as the world, but there was no room in it to hold the memory of a wrong.
source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Letters and Social Aims (1876), Greatness
sourceRaw: [[Ralph Waldo Emerson]], ''Letters and Social Aims'' (1876), ''Greatness''
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
textKo: 그의 마음은 세상만큼 컸으나, 그 안에 원한의 기억이 들어설 자리는 없었다.

text: Bear and forbear.
source: Epictetus. See Gellius, Book XVII. 6
sourceRaw: [[Epictetus]]. See Gellius, Book XVII. 6
author: Epictetus
textKo: 견디고, 절제하라.

text: If you made a mistake in the past and learn from it now, you are using clock time. On the other hand, if you dwell on it mentally, and self-criticism, remorse, or guilt come up, then you are making the mistake into “me” and “mine”: you make it part of your sense of self, and it has become psychological time, which is always linked to a false sense of identity.
source: Eckhart Tolle The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment (1997)
sourceRaw: [[Eckhart Tolle]] [[The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment|''The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment'']] (1997)
author: Eckhart Tolle
textKo: 과거의 실수에서 지금 배우고 있다면 너는 '시계 시간'을 사용하고 있는 것이다. 그러나 그것에 정신적으로 머무르며 자책·후회·죄책감이 일어난다면, 너는 그 실수를 '나'와 '내 것'으로 만들고 있다. 너의 자아감의 일부로 만들었기에, 그것은 거짓된 정체감과 항상 연결된 '심리적 시간'이 되어버린다.

text: Forgiveness of the present is even more important than forgiveness of the past. If you forgive every moment - allow it to be as it is - then there will be no accumulation of resentment that needs to be forgiven at some later time... It seems that most people need to experience a great deal of suffering before they will relinquish resistance and accept - before they will forgive. As soon as they do, one of the greatest miracles happens: the awakening of Being -consciousness through what appears as evil, the transmutation of suffering into inner peace. The ultimate effect of all the evil and suffering in the world is that it will force humans into realizing who they are beyond name and form. Thus, what we perceive as evil from our limited perspective is actually part of the higher good that has no opposite. This, however, does not become true for you except through forgiveness. Until that happens, evil has not been redeemed and therefore remains evil.
source: Eckhart Tolle The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment (1997)
sourceRaw: [[Eckhart Tolle]] [[The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment|''The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment'']] (1997)
author: Eckhart Tolle
textKo: 현재의 용서가 과거의 용서보다 더 중요하다. 매 순간을 용서한다면 — 그 순간이 있는 그대로 존재하도록 허용한다면 — 훗날 용서해야 할 원한이 쌓이지 않는다. 대부분의 사람은 저항을 내려놓고 받아들이기 — 곧 용서하기 — 전에 많은 고통을 겪어야 하는 듯하다. 그렇게 할 때 가장 큰 기적 중 하나가 일어난다: 악으로 보이는 것을 통한 '존재' 의식의 깨어남, 고통이 내면의 평화로 변모되는 것이다.

text: Through forgiveness, which essentially means recognizing the insubstantiality of the past and allowing the present moment to be as it is, the miracle of transformation happens not only within but also without. A silent space of intense presence arises both in you and around you. Whoever or whatever enters that field of consciousness will be affected by it, sometimes visibly and immediately, sometimes at deeper levels with visible changes appearing at a later time. You dissolve discord, heal pain, dispel unconsciousness - without doing anything - simply by being and holding that frequency of intense presence.
source: Eckhart Tolle The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment (1997)
sourceRaw: [[Eckhart Tolle]] [[The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment|''The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment'']] (1997)
author: Eckhart Tolle
textKo: 용서를 통해 — 본질적으로 과거의 무실체성을 인식하고 현재의 순간이 있는 그대로이게 허용함을 통해 — 변모의 기적은 너의 안뿐 아니라 바깥에서도 일어난다. 강렬한 현존의 고요한 공간이 너의 안과 주위에 일어난다. 그 의식의 장에 들어오는 누구든 무엇이든 영향을 받는다 — 때로는 즉시 가시적으로, 때로는 더 깊은 차원에서 시간이 흐른 뒤 변화로 나타난다. 너는 아무것도 하지 않고 그저 존재하면서 그 강렬한 현존의 진동을 유지함으로써 불화를 녹이고, 고통을 치유하고, 무의식을 흩어버린다.

text: "Forgiveness" is a term that has been in use for 2,000 years, but most people have a very limited view of what it means. You cannot truly forgive yourself or others as long as you derive your sense of self from the past. Only through accessing the power of the Now, which is your own power, can there be true forgiveness. This renders the past powerless, and you realize deeply that nothing you ever did or that was ever done to you could touch even in the slightest the radiant essence of who you are. The whole concept of forgiveness then becomes unnecessary.... When you surrender to what is and so become fully present, the past ceases to have any power. You do not need it anymore. Presence is the key. The Now is the key.
source: Eckhart Tolle The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment (1997)
sourceRaw: [[Eckhart Tolle]] [[The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment|''The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment'']] (1997)
author: Eckhart Tolle
textKo: '용서'는 2000년간 쓰여 온 말이지만, 대부분의 사람은 그 의미를 매우 제한적으로 본다. 너의 자아감을 과거에서 끌어내는 한, 너는 자신도 타인도 진정으로 용서할 수 없다. 오직 '지금'의 힘 — 너 자신의 힘 — 에 접속할 때만 참된 용서가 가능하다. 이것은 과거를 무력하게 만들고, 네가 행하거나 너에게 행해진 그 어떤 것도 너의 본질의 빛나는 정수를 조금도 건드릴 수 없다는 것을 깊이 깨닫게 한다. 그러면 '용서'라는 개념 자체가 불필요해진다... 있는 그대로에 항복하여 온전히 현존할 때, 과거는 더 이상 어떤 힘도 갖지 못한다. 현존이 열쇠다. '지금'이 열쇠다.

text: I worked with patience which means almost power.
source: Elizabeth Barrett Browning, Aurora Leigh (1856), Book III, line 205.
sourceRaw: [[Elizabeth Barrett Browning]], ''Aurora Leigh'' (1856), Book III, line 205.
workTitle: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
author: Elizabeth Barrett Browning
sectionPath: Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations
textKo: 나는 인내로 일했다. 그것은 거의 힘과 같은 것이다.

text: Never think that God's delays are God's denials. Hold on! hold fast! hold out! Patience is genius.
source: Count De Buffon, p. 444.
sourceRaw: [[Count De Buffon]], p. 444.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Count De Buffon
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 신의 지체가 곧 신의 거절이라고 결코 생각지 마라. 붙들라! 굳건히 잡으라! 견뎌내라! 인내는 천재성이다.

text: A true Christian man is distinguished from other men, not so much by his beneficent works, as by his patience.
source: Horace Bushnell, p. 442.
sourceRaw: [[Horace Bushnell]], p. 442.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Horace Bushnell
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 참된 그리스도인이 다른 사람과 구별되는 것은 그 선행보다도 그 인내에 의해서다.

text: Christ commands you to take up His cross and follow Him, not that He may humble you, or lay some penance upon you, but that you may surrender the low self-will and the feeble pride of your sin, and ascend into the sublime patience of heavenly charity.
source: Horace Bushnell, p. 443.
sourceRaw: [[Horace Bushnell]], p. 443.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Horace Bushnell
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 그리스도가 네게 자기 십자가를 지고 따르라 명하신 것은 너를 굴복시키거나 무슨 보속을 지우려 함이 아니다. 다만 죄의 비루한 자기 의지와 미약한 교만을 내려놓고, 천상 사랑의 숭고한 인내로 오르게 하시려 함이다.

text: It is not necessary for all men to be great in action. The greatest and sublimest power is often simple patience.
source: Horace Bushnell, p. 443.
sourceRaw: [[Horace Bushnell]], p. 443.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Horace Bushnell
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 모든 사람이 행동에서 위대할 필요는 없다. 가장 위대하고 숭고한 힘은 흔히 단순한 인내다.

text: Teach me to feel that Thou art always nigh;Teach me the struggles of the soul to bear;To check the rising doubt, the rebel sigh;Teach me the patience of unanswered prayer.
source: George Croly, p. 444.
sourceRaw: [[George Croly]], p. 444.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: George Croly
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 제게 가르치소서 — 당신이 늘 가까이 계심을 느끼게 하시고, 영혼의 분투를 견디는 법, 일어나는 의심과 반항의 한숨을 누르는 법, 응답 없는 기도의 인내를 가르치소서.

text: Patience! why, it is the soul of peace; of all the virtues it is nearest kin to heaven; it makes men look like gods. The best of men that ever wore earth about Him was a Sufferer,— a soft, meek, patient, humble, tranquil spirit; the first true gentleman that ever breathed.
source: Thomas Decker, p. 443.
sourceRaw: [[Thomas Decker]], p. 443.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Thomas Decker
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 인내여! 그것이야말로 평화의 영혼이다. 모든 덕 중에서 그것은 천국에 가장 가까운 친족이며, 사람을 신처럼 보이게 한다. 일찍이 흙을 입은 가장 훌륭한 분도 고난받는 자, 부드럽고 온유하며 인내심 깊고 겸손하고 평온한 영혼 — 일찍이 숨 쉰 가장 참된 신사 — 이셨다.

text: Dispose thyself to patience rather than to comfort, and to the bearing of the cross rather than to gladness.
source: Thomas à Kempis, p. 442.
sourceRaw: [[Thomas à Kempis]], p. 442.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Thomas à Kempis
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 위안보다 인내에 너 자신을 두고, 기쁨보다 십자가 짊을 받아들이라.

text: The holier one is, the more forbearing and loving he is; the more tender and patient and anxious to help others in every way. Think how forbearing and loving Christ is when we do wrong; and there we are to be like Him.
source: Arthur Henry Kenney, p. 444.
sourceRaw: [[Arthur Henry Kenney]], p. 444.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Arthur Henry Kenney
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 거룩한 자일수록 더 너그럽고 사랑이 많으며, 더 부드럽고 인내심 깊으며, 모든 면에서 남을 돕고자 더 애쓴다. 우리가 잘못할 때 그리스도가 얼마나 너그럽고 사랑 많으신지 생각해보라. 우리도 그분을 본받아야 한다.

text: Therefore, let us be patient, patient; and let God our Father teach His own lesson, His own way. Let us try to learn it well and quickly; but do not let us fancy that He will ring the school-bell, and send us to play before our lesson is learnt.
source: Charles Kingsley, p. 443.
sourceRaw: [[Charles Kingsley]], p. 443.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Charles Kingsley
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 그러니 친구들이여, 인내하고 또 인내하라. 아버지 신께서 자기 방식으로 자기 가르침을 친히 가르치시도록 두라. 그것을 잘, 빨리 배우도록 애쓰되, 우리의 가르침이 다 배우기도 전에 신께서 종을 울려 놀러 보내실 것이라 착각하지는 말자.

text: Be patient, my friends; time rolls rapidly away; our longing has its end. The hour will strike, who knows how soon?— when the maternal lap of everlasting Love shall be opened to us, and the full peace of God breathe around us from the palmy summits of Eden.
source: Friedrich Wilhelm Krummacher, p. 613.
sourceRaw: [[Friedrich Wilhelm Krummacher]], p. 613.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Friedrich Wilhelm Krummacher
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 인내하라, 내 친구들이여. 시간은 빠르게 흐르고, 우리의 갈망도 끝이 있다. 그 시간이 — 얼마나 빨리 올지는 누가 알겠는가 — 울릴 것이다. 영원한 사랑의 어머니 같은 품이 우리에게 열리고, 신의 충만한 평화가 에덴의 종려나무 정상에서 우리를 둘러쌀 그 시간이.

text: We are waiting, Master, waiting,Wayworn, pressed with toils and strife;Waiting, hoping, watching, praying,Till we reach the gates of life.
source: Ray Palmer, p. 613.
sourceRaw: [[Ray Palmer]], p. 613.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Ray Palmer
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 우리는 기다리고 있나이다, 주님이여. 지치고, 수고와 다툼에 눌려 — 기다리고, 소망하고, 지켜보고, 기도하며, 생명의 문에 이르기까지.

text: Show yourself a Christian by suffering without murmuring. In patience possess your soul — they lose nothing who gain Christ.
source: Samuel Rutherford, p. 444.
sourceRaw: [[Samuel Rutherford]], p. 444.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Samuel Rutherford
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 불평 없이 고난을 견딤으로써 그리스도인임을 보이라. 인내로 너의 영혼을 보존하라 — 그리스도를 얻는 자는 아무것도 잃지 않는다.

text: The disciples of a patient Saviour should be patient themselves.
source: Charles Spurgeon, p. 442.
sourceRaw: [[Charles Spurgeon]], p. 442.
workTitle: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers
author: Charles Spurgeon
sectionPath: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895)
textKo: 인내하신 구주의 제자들은 그 자신도 인내해야 한다.

text: 'This is an attachment; here there is little happiness, and little satisfaction; here there is very much misery; this is a hook.' Knowing this, a thoughtful man should wander solitary as a rhinoceros horn.Having torn one's fetters asunder, like a fish breaking a net in the water, not returning, like a fire not going back to what is already burned, one should wander solitary as a rhinoceros horn.
source: Gautama Buddha, Sutta Nipata, The Group of Discourses, K. R. Norman, trans. (Oxford: 2001)
sourceRaw: [[Gautama Buddha]], ''Sutta Nipata'', The Group of Discourses, K. R. Norman, trans. (Oxford: 2001)
author: Gautama Buddha
textKo: '이것은 집착이다. 여기엔 행복도 만족도 적고, 비참함만 많다. 이것은 갈고리다.' 이를 아는 사려 깊은 자는 무소뿔처럼 홀로 거닐어야 한다. 족쇄를 끊은 자는, 물속에서 그물을 찢는 물고기처럼, 이미 타버린 것에 다시 돌아가지 않는 불처럼, 무소뿔처럼 홀로 거닐어야 한다.

text: We never touch but at points.
source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Journals (1836)
sourceRaw: [[Ralph Waldo Emerson]], ''Journals'' (1836)
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
textKo: 우리는 결코 닿지 않는다, 오직 점에서만 닿을 뿐이다.

text: What I must do is all that concerns me, not what the people think. This rule, equally arduous in actual & in intellectual life, may serve for the whole distinction between greatness & meanness. It is the harder because you will always find those who think they know what is your duty better than you know it. It is easy in the world to live after the world's opinion; it is easy in solitude to live after our own; but the great man is he who in the midst of the crowd keeps with perfect sweetness the independence of solitude.
source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Essays: First Series, Self-Reliance (1841)
sourceRaw: [[Ralph Waldo Emerson]],  ''[[Ralph_Waldo_Emerson#Self-Reliance|Essays: First Series, Self-Reliance]]'' (1841)
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
textKo: 내가 해야 할 일은 오직 내가 할 일이지, 사람들이 어떻게 생각하느냐가 아니다. 이 규율은 실제 삶에서도 지적 삶에서도 똑같이 어려우나, 위대함과 비루함의 전 차이를 가른다. 이는 더욱 어려운데, 네 의무가 무엇인지 너보다 더 잘 안다고 여기는 자들이 늘 있기 때문이다. 군중 가운데서도 고독의 독립성을 완벽한 평온함으로 지키는 자, 그가 위대한 사람이다.

text: It is simpler to be self-dependent. The height, the deity of man is, to be self-sustained, to need no gift, no foreign force. Society is good when it does not violate me; but best when it is likest to solitude.
source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, "The Transcendentalist" (January 1842)
sourceRaw: [[Ralph Waldo Emerson]], "[[w:The Transcendentalist|The Transcendentalist]]" (January 1842)
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
textKo: 스스로에게 의존하는 것이 더 단순하다. 인간의 높이, 인간의 신성함은 자족하는 것, 어떤 선물도 어떤 외부의 힘도 필요로 하지 않는 것에 있다. 사회는 나를 침해하지 않을 때 좋고, 고독에 가장 가까울 때 가장 좋다.

text: We dress our garden, eat our dinners, discuss the household with our wives, and these things make no impression, are forgotten next week; but, in the solitude to which every man is always returning, he has a sanity and revelations which in his passage into new worlds he will carry with him. Never mind the ridicule, never mind the defeat; up again, old heart!—it seems to say—there is victory yet for all justice; and the true romance which the world exists to realize will be the transformation of genius into practical power.
source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Essays: Second Series, Experience (1844)
sourceRaw: [[Ralph Waldo Emerson]], ''[[Ralph Waldo Emerson#Experience|Essays: Second Series, Experience]]'' (1844)
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
textKo: 우리는 정원을 가꾸고 저녁을 먹고 아내와 집안일을 이야기하지만, 이것들은 인상을 남기지 못해 다음 주면 잊힌다. 그러나 모든 이가 늘 돌아가는 고독 속에서, 그는 새 세계로 옮겨갈 때 함께 지니고 갈 분별과 계시를 얻는다. 비웃음에도, 패배에도 신경 쓰지 마라. 다시 일어나라, 늙은 마음이여! — 모든 정의에는 아직 승리가 있고, 세상이 실현하기 위해 존재하는 진실한 로맨스는 천재가 실천력으로 변모하는 일임을 말해주는 듯하다.

text: This is that which we call character,—a reserved force which acts directly by presence, and without means. It is conceived of as a certain undemonstrable force, a Familiar or Genius, by whose impulses the man is guided but whose counsels he cannot impart; which is company for him, so that such men are often solitary, or if they choose to be social, do not need society but can entertain themselves very well alone.
source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Essays: Second Series (1844), III. Character
sourceRaw: [[Ralph Waldo Emerson]], ''Essays: Second Series'' (1844), III. Character
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
textKo: 이것이 우리가 '인격'이라 부르는 것이다 — 존재 자체로 직접 작용하는, 수단 없는 비축된 힘이다. 그것은 입증할 수 없는 어떤 힘, '내면의 정령' 혹은 '천재'로 인식되며, 그 충동에 의해 인간은 인도되지만 그 조언을 남에게 전할 수는 없다. 그것이 그에게 동반자가 되어주므로, 그런 사람들은 흔히 고독을 즐기거나, 사교를 택하더라도 사회를 필요로 하지 않고 홀로도 즐겁게 지낸다.

text: When you have shut your doors, and darkened your room, remember never to say that you are alone; for you are not alone, but God is within, and your genius is within; and what need have they of light to see what you are doing?
source: Epictetus, Discourses, Book I, ch. xiv, trans. Thomas Wentworth Higginson in The Works of Epictetus, Vol. I (Boston: Little, Brown and Company, 1890), p. 54
sourceRaw: [[Epictetus]], ''Discourses'', Book I, ch. xiv, trans. Thomas Wentworth Higginson in ''The Works of Epictetus'', Vol. I (Boston: Little, Brown and Company, 1890), p. 54
author: Epictetus
textKo: 문을 닫고 방을 어둡게 했을 때, 결코 혼자라고 말하지 마라. 너는 혼자가 아니라 신이 안에 계시고, 너의 정령이 안에 있다. 그분들이 네가 하는 일을 보시는데 빛이 무엇 때문에 필요하겠는가?

text: Oh, for a lodge in some vast wilderness,Some boundless contiguity of shade,Where rumour of oppression and deceit,Of unsuccessful or successful war,Might never reach me more!
source: William Cowper, The Task (1785), Book II, line 1
sourceRaw: [[William Cowper]], ''The Task'' (1785), Book II, line 1

author: William Cowper

textKo: 오, 어느 광활한 황야의 오두막이여, 그늘이 끝없이 이어지는 곳, 압제와 기만의 풍문도, 패전이든 승전이든 전쟁의 소식도, 다시는 내게 닿지 못할 그곳이여!

text: Solitude is the nurse of enthusiasm, and enthusiasm is the true parent of genius. In all ages solitude has been called for—has been flown to.
source: Isaac D'Israeli, The Literary Character, Illustrated by the History of Men of Genius (1795-1822), Chapter X
sourceRaw: [[Isaac D'Israeli]], ''The Literary Character, Illustrated by the History of Men of Genius'' (1795-1822), Chapter X

textKo: 고독은 열정의 유모이며, 열정은 천재의 참된 부모다. 어느 시대에나 고독은 찾는 자가 있었고, 도피처가 되어왔다.

text: There is a society in the deepest solitude.
source: Isaac D'Israeli, The Literary Character, Illustrated by the History of Men of Genius (1795-1822), Chapter X
sourceRaw: [[Isaac D'Israeli]], ''The Literary Character, Illustrated by the History of Men of Genius'' (1795-1822), Chapter X

source: Charles Stewart Parnell, Speech at Ennis (19 September 1880)
sourceRaw: [[Charles Stewart Parnell]], ''Speech at Ennis'' (19 September 1880)

text: I never found the companion that was so companionable as solitude.
source: Henry David Thoreau, Solitude
sourceRaw: [[Henry David Thoreau]], ''Solitude''

text: Fire is the test of gold; adversity, of strong men.
source: Seneca the Younger, De Providentia, 5, 9.
sourceRaw: [[Seneca the Younger]], ''[[w:De Providentia|De Providentia]]'', 5, 9.
author: Seneca the Younger
textKo: 불은 황금을 시험하고, 역경은 강한 사람을 시험한다.

text: Let me embrace thee, sour adversity,For wise men say it is the wisest course.
source: William Shakespeare, Henry VI, Part III (c. 1591), Act III, scene 1, line 24.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], [[Henry VI, Part 3|''Henry VI'', Part III]] (c. 1591), Act III, scene 1, line 24.

textKo: 쓰디쓴 역경이여, 너를 끌어안으리. 현자들은 그것이 가장 지혜로운 길이라 말하니.

text: His overthrow heap'd happiness upon him;For then, and not till then, he felt himself,And found the blessedness of being little.
source: William Shakespeare, Henry VIII (c. 1613), Act IV, scene 2, line 64.
sourceRaw: [[William Shakespeare]], ''[[Henry VIII (play)|Henry VIII]]'' ([[w:Henry VIII (play)#Date|c. 1613]]), Act IV, scene 2, line 64.
